And Shlomo strengthened himself because Hashem his Elokim was with him.

And Shlomo said to all Yisrael And who were those referred to as “all Yisrael”? They were the leaders of the thousands, as it is written (Divrei Hayamim I 28:1): “And David assembled all the leaders of Yisrael.” And what did he say to them? That they should come with him to the high place that was in Givon.

And Shlomo and the entire assembly with him, etc. It is customary for Scripture to abbreviate, [as we find:] (Yonah 2:11): “And Hashem said to the fish, and it spewed Yonah onto the dry land,” and similarly (Divrei Hayamim I 21:27): “And Hashem said to the angel, and his sword was returned to its sheath.”
Request, what shall I give you Choose and request all that you desire, and I shall grant it to you.
Now, O Hashem Elokim, may...come true - Heb. יֵאָמֵן, (provarsi in Italian), to prove (true).

for You have enthroned me Since You have enthroned me over a numerous people like this, I require wisdom and strength to go forth before them and to wage their wars, as it is stated (Shmuel I 8:20): “and our king will judge us and wage our wars.” Now since I must ask what is in my heart, I shall ask what I require and that is that You grant me wisdom.

and I shall go forth before this people and come in And also, a king requires a wise heart to know how to judge, and I am young and tender. Even a thousand wise men would have difficulty judging such a large nation, because it is impossible that they should not have many disputes, which they come to litigate, and he has no time to deliberate on their case, for while this one is complaining and does not stop talking, another one comes and cries. Now who can decide a thousand legal decisions in one day, except one who is wise and astute, endowed with the spirit of Elokim? Therefore, this I request, that You give me wisdom and knowledge to judge this great people of Yours, for this is what I require that You give me.

Since this was in your heart For a person does not request this thing unless he has the fear of Heaven in his heart, as it is stated (Shemot 18:21): “But you must seek out from the people men of ability, Elokim-fearing men.”
the life of your enemies to defeat them.
Wisdom and knowledge are granted you that which you requested.
and riches, possessions, and honor which you did not request, I shall grant you.

such as that the kings before you did not possess and which will not be so after you This refers back to “riches and honor” which you did not request, because the wisdom that I am granting you: riches, honor, and longevity, are dependent on it, as it is written (Mishlei 3:16): “Length of days in its right hand; and in its left hand, riches and honor.” This is what is written (Melachim I 10:23): Now King Shlomo transcended all the kings of the earth in affluence and wisdom, etc.”

and he left them in the chariot cities He left some of those horsemen and chariots in the chariot cities; since the king’s chariots were there, those cities were called the chariot cities, and some of them he left with him in Yerushalayim.

like stones Because of the abundance of silver and gold that he had, he was not particular about distributing silver and gold throughout the city to make tables and chairs. Our Rabbis said (Ecc. Rabbah 2:3): Like stones of ten or eight cubits: just as he cut stones, so did he cut silver.
And Shlomo’s source of horses i.e., Shlomo’s entire source of horses was exclusively from Mitzrayim.
and [there was] an assemblage from which the king’s agents - Heb. מִקְוֵה, the assemblage of the horses in Mitzrayim, and it is called stutte in Middle High German.
to devote to Him for some purpose.
to burn before Him incense which is a way of honor[ing Him], and this is repeated further (verse 5): “but to burn incense before Him.”

making this permanent over Yisrael Therefore, I request of you to send to me [material] for a good and strong House, because it is required perpetually for Yisrael to offer up their sacrifice(s) in this House, which I am building.

And the House, which I am building, is great Therefore, I require of you to send me of your buildings. Now if you say, “Make the House smaller, so that you will not need other people,” I cannot do so, because our Elokim is greater than all Gods; therefore, I cannot diminish it or make it smaller.

And who can gather up strength to build Him a house Since he said, “And the House which I am building is great,” perhaps [you may think that] this will mean “great enough for His needs,” but this is not so, for “who can gather strength?” For who can compress and gather his strength enough to build a house fit for Him? An example of this appears above (Divrei Hayamim I 29:14): “that we should gather up strength to donate.”

for the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain Him Therefore, he says, “and who am I, to build Him a House?” And that which I am building Him is nothing more than to burn incense therein before Him.
and with purple אַרְגְּוָן. This is synonymous with אַרְגָּמָן.
and crimson כַּרְמִיל. This is תוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי. The proof is that תוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי is not mentioned here.

and who knows how to make engravings Heb. לְפַתֵּחַ פִּתּוּחִים. An example is (Shemot 28:36) פִּתּוּחֵי חֹתָם, the engravings of a signet; someone who knows how to cut and make forms in stones, graber or greber in Middle German.
Abundant wheat - Heb. מַכּוֹת, in Middle High German vollauff, in abundance, and some say that מַכּוֹת means crushed to extract the wheat kernels from the ear.
and wine twenty thousand baths The expression of bath refers to a liquid measure, and kor is a dry measure.
endowed with understanding, of my father Churam He was my father’s ingenious craftsman, and he is also mine.
the son of a woman She was a widow.
of the daughters of Dan of the tribe of Dan.

and his father was a Tzori man He was a Yehudi who lived in Tzor, on the model of (Shmuel II 6:10): “Obed-Edom the Giti,” who lived in Gat, and who was a Levi. In Melachim I (7:14), it is written: “He was a widow’s son, of the tribe of Naftali, and his father was a Tzori man.” His mother was from Dan, and his father was from Naftali. Now why was it necessary to trace his genealogy, from which tribe his father and mother were? This is what is written (Bereshit 30:6): “Elokim judged me,” and also (ibid. 8): “I have fought a divine struggle, etc.” Rachel said, “I twisted cords; I went through contortions until I was able to compare to my sister Leah. If Leah will boast of her descendant Betzalel, who will make the Tabernacle, he will require one of the sons of Dan to participate in his work, as it is written (38: 23): ‘And with him was Oholiav the son of Achisamach of the tribe of Dan.’ Now if Shlomo, the descendant of my sister, will build the Temple, some of the sons of Dan and Naftali will have to participate with him.”

and his father was a Tzori man [This comes] to teach you that even if his mother is a widow, a person must adopt his father’s trade and sustain his mother. (So I heard from Rabbi Shlomo the son of Levi of Monteuille, the son of Rabbi Moshe Hadarshan’s sister.)
as rafts - Heb. רַפְסדוֹת, and in Melachim I (5:23) it is written: דבְרוֹת, in Middle High German vloeze, rafts, (in modern German flüsse).
on the sea of Yafo meaning on the seacoast, like (Yonah 1:3): “and he went down to Yafo.”

And Shlomo counted all the strangers who were in the land of Yisrael - Heb. הַגֵּירִים. This is written with the plene spelling, two yuds. In the beginning, when David counted them (Divrei Hayamim I 22:2), they were called הַגֵּרִים with one yud, but Shlomo counted them at the time of the deed, when he built; therefore, it is written with the plene spelling. A similar instance: “then you shall bring up my bones from this place.” “With you” is missing in the portion of וַיְחִי (Bereshit 50:25), but at the time of the deed (in the portion of בְּשַׁלַּח, Shemot 13:19), when he took them, it is written: “with you.”
And Shlomo counted, etc., after the census above (Divrei Hayamim I 22:2), as it is written: “And David ordered to gather the strangers.”

And he made of them seventy thousand, etc. The reason he mentions them again and mentions the number is that he interrupted the topic; therefore, he had to repeat it again now. And he did not stop until he finished the entire [account of the] building, and he says immediately (3:1): “And Shlomo commenced to build, etc.” Now, even with one verse, it is customary to interrupt the topic and [then] to begin [again] with the previous statement, e.g., (Bamidbar 16:6): “Do this: take yourself, etc.” And the morrow, it says (ibid. 16f.): “And Moshe said to Korach: You and all your band, etc.,” and he repeats and says, “and let each man take his censer and place, etc.” Since he interrupted with many verses, it was necessary to rewrite it, and how much more so here.
on Mount Moriyah because the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to David in the threshing floor of Ornan when the plague stopped, and that is Mount Moriyah, David’s place.

And he commenced to build in the second month This is explained at the beginning of Tractate Rosh Hashanah Yerushalmi (1:1), and the meaning is: the second of Iyar. Since he wished to say, “in the fourth year of his reign,” he had to repeat and say, “in the second.” A similar instance is (Bereshit 8: 5): “And the waters continued to diminish until the tenth month, etc.” Another similar instance is (Melachim I 6:1): “in the fourth year in the month Ziv, which was the second month of Shlomo’s reign, etc.” This refers back to “the fourth year,” and then in the fourth year of his reign he commenced in the second [month], because all the days of the winter he could not [build] because of the cold, and in Nissan he could not [build] because of Passover.

the length in cubits, in the first measure And since he interrupted and said “in the first measure,” he says again, “cubits,” i.e., the cubit length of the House was sixty cubits, including the Dvir and the Heichal, and the breadth was twenty cubits.

And the vestibule, the length of which was The length of the vestibule, opposite the breadth of the House, was twenty, for the length of the vestibule, which was opposite the breadth of the House, was twenty cubits from north to south, and every larger dimension is called length, and the smaller one is called breadth, and since in the Heichal, its measurement from east to west is larger and from north to south is smaller, it is called the breadth, but in the vestibule, whose measurement from north to south is larger, it is called the length, and its measurement from east to west, which is smaller, is called the breadth, and the breadth of the vestibule was ten cubits, as is delineated in Melachim I (6:3): “ten cubits was the breadth thereof before the House.”

and the height was one hundred and twenty But in Melachim I (6:2), it is written: “and thirty cubits the height thereof.” How so? The height of the [first] floor from the floor of the house to the ceiling of the first upper story was thirty cubits, and from upper story to upper story up to the highest roof was ninety cubits, as is written: (Divrei Hayamim I 28:11): “And David gave his son Shlomo the pattern of the vestibule and its houses and its treasures and its upper stories.” From there it can be deduced that there were upper stories there.

and he overlaid it from within with pure gold The inside of the Heichal, which was the greater house, he overlaid with gold, but not the vestibule, and he proceeds and delineates further how he did it. And the greater House He overlaid the entire House with pure gold. he overlaid with juniper wood - Heb. עֲצֵי בְרוֹשִּׁים. [This translation follows Yehudah Feliks, Nature & Man in the Bible, pp.110f.] For the entire House, the Dvir and the Heichal, he first overlaid with juniper wood, and afterwards, “he overlaid it with fine gold” over the walls of juniper, and because of the overlaying of gold, with which he wished to overlay the House, he overlaid it first with wood in order that the gold would adhere firmly, for he would reinforce the gold with nails, with the decorations of the wood, for he made decorations in the wood. palm trees - Heb. תִּמּרִים. They are trees like a sort of palm trees and cherubim, and in Melachim I (6:32) it is written: “and he carved upon them carvings of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers (וּפְטוּרֵי צִצִּים),” like (Bamidbar 17:23) “and it sprouted fruit (וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ)”. And פְטוּרֵי is like “A man frees (פּוֹטֵר) his wife (entwerfen in Middle High German). (From Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Meshulam of blessed memory.)

and he overlaid it with gold i.e., When he made all the decorations, he overlaid the walls with gold after the decorations, and he reinforced them with nails in the wooden wall, in order that it should not move; which is something that he could not do on a stone wall. For this reason, he overlaid the entire House with juniper wood.

and chains He made many decorations, filling it completely, and when he saw that there was any blank space between one decoration and another, he painted a decoration like a sort of chain, with which things are connected, so did he do here between one decoration and another, in order that there should be no blank space in between. Another interpretation is that he made real golden chains and connected the shapes together with them.
And he overlaid the House with precious stone He set and inlaid precious stones in gold in the walls of the House for glory and for beauty.

and the gold that he refers to: “and he overlaid it with fine gold,” was of the gold of Parvayim. Parvayim is the name of a place, and our Sages explained that it resembles the blood of bulls in its high quality and its redness.
And he overlaid - Heb. וַיְחַף like וַיְצַף, and he explains what he overlaid in the Housethe walls and the sideposts.

and its walls [i.e., the walls] of the sideposts of the House, which were [made] of stones, and he explains: “its walls and its doors with gold.” In Melachim I (6:15) it says: “until the walls of the ceiling (קִירוֹת הַסִּפֻּן).” Now this is why he calls the roof קִירוֹת הַסִּפֻּן, because the roof was like an inverted ship (סְפִינָה) or boat, for it is customary to make the ceiling round, like a ship.

And he made the House of, etc. This is what he should have said: “And he made the house of the Holy of Holies twenty by twenty,” [since neither side was longer] but because he said above (verse 4): “And the vestibule, etc. opposite the breadth of the House, was twenty cubits, etc.,” he words it similarly here.

and he overlaid it with fine gold Also in the Holy of Holies, he first built walls of wood, and upon it he overlaid gold, and the reason he does not mention any wood here in the Holy of Holies is due to the greatness of the Temple; i.e., all the walls of the House of the Ark were of gold, and there was no wood in them, and that was honor for the Holy of Holies, and this is proven in Kings (ad loc.). The proof that because of the honor of the House he does not mention any wood is that it is written (verse 6): “And he overlaid the House with precious stone,” whereas in Kings, it is not written: “precious stone.” Why not? Because in the Book of the Divrei Hayamim of the Kings of Yehudah he lets you know that Shlomo’s intention was for the honor of the House.
And the weight of the nails to reinforce with them the gold on the wooden walls.
in shekels in the weight of shekels, fifty shekels of gold.

with the appearance of children - Heb. צַעֲצֻעִים. A similar instance is (Yeshayahu 22:24): הַצֶּאֱצָאִים וְהַצְּפִעוֹת, which is translated by the Targum as: the children, etc. He made the form of boys and girls for cherubim, [based on the Aramaic] כְּרַבְיָא, [meaning like children,] and they were of wood, which he afterwards overlaid with gold, and in Melachim I (6:23): “And he made in the Dvir two cherubim of olive wood,” but all that was within of wood he does not wish to mention in this Book because of its honor.

And the wings of the cherubim - their length was twenty cubits How so? The wing of one was five cubits, and the end of the five reached the wall of the House to the south, and the other wing reached the wing of the other cherub, which was at its side, totaling ten cubits for one cherub, and so for the other one. It is found that the wing of one cherub reached the north, and the wing of one cherub reached the south. It follows that they were as long as the entire western wall, which was twenty cubits [long]. And concerning their bodies, our Sages said, (Yoma 21a), that they stood miraculously, [i.e., they did not occupy space]. But according to the simple explanation of the matter, it appears to me that their bodies protruded from them like a bird which spreads its wings, that its body protrudes outside its wings, (See B.B. 99a) and their height is delineated in Melachim I (6:26): “The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was that of the second cherub.”
standing on their feet on the floor of the House to the west.

with their faces to the House To the inside, for their heads were not erect, so that they should appear as though looking outward, but their heads were bent and looking before them, as it is written (Shemot 25:20): “and their faces [shall be] one toward the other,” but here it says. “with their faces to the House,” but rather their heads were facing each other, and their heads were also bent toward the House, toward the inside, and the Ark was standing in the place of the wing spread of the two cherubim, and the wings of the cherubim were inclined from the wall and shielded the Ark cover and the Ark with their wings. Aside from these cherubim were the cherubim that Moshe had made from the Ark cover, still attached and clinging to the Ark cover and standing upon it. Do not be surprised about this, because likewise, Shlomo made ten tables and ten candelabra, besides those of Moshe.

And he made the dividing curtain of blue, purple and he hung it on the door that was in the cubit between the two partitions, through which they would enter the Holy of Holies. Although it had doors, he hung it upon it as further (4:22): “And the entrance to the House, its inner doors to the Holy of Holies, etc.”
and he wrought cherubim into it pictures of cherubim.

thirty-five cubits long i.e., the height. And in Melachim I (7:15): “And he cast the two pillars of copper, eighteen cubits, etc.” Rabbi Shlomo (Rashi to Kings) explained that he cast them both together and subsequently divided them in two, and the missing cubit is not counted because it is unlike the work of the rest of the pillar, as is written there in the section (7:22): “And upon the top of the pillars was lily work.” Rabbi Yosef [Kara] also explained it in this manner, but it is not acceptable to me, for what is the meaning of its height being eighteen, but this is how I heard it, that he surely cast them both together, and then divided them in two; so we find that each one was seventeen and a half cubits, and the capital, which was the chapiter, as is stated there, its thickness was half a cubit, making each one eighteen cubits.

and the capital - Heb. וְהַצֶּפֶת. That is the overlay (צִפּוּי) like (verse 10): “and he (sic) overlaid them (וַיְצַפֶּה) with gold.” I.e., it was made like a sort of hollow (conical) hat, whose thickness was half of a cubit from below, and when it is inverted and placed on the pillar, it is found to be eighteen cubits: in Melachim I (7:16-20), it is called chapiters (כֹּתָרוֹת), an expression of a crown (כֶּתֶר), as it is written: “And two chapiters (כּתָרוֹת), etc.”

and placed them in the chains He made chains at the top of the capital under it, and within the chains he set forms of pomegranates in order to cover the hollow of the capital, as it is written (ibid. verse 41): “to cover the two bowls (גֻלּוֹת) of the chapiters,” and because of its hollow, he calls them גֻלּוֹת. And concerning the net-work (שְׂבָכָה) written there, these are the chains, an expression of (Iyov 18:8): “and he shall walk on the nets (שְׂבָכָה),” an expression of branches, like (Bereshit 22:13): “caught in the hedge (בַּסְּבַךְ) by its horns.” Some interpret it as coif, and Rabbi Eliezer interprets it as branches.

before the Heichal At the entrance of the Heichal on the outside, in the vestibule, as is proven in Melachim I (7:19): “And the chapiters that were upon the top of the pillars were of lily work in the vestibule.”
one from the right of the entrance.
and one from the left of the entrance.
Yachin, etc. Boaz Yachin because of the kingdom of the house of David, which was compared to the moon, as it is written (Tehillim 89:38): “Like the moon, which is established (יִכּוֹן) forever.”

Boaz, corresponding to the sun, [which emerges with might and strength (עֹז) (Yesod Veshoresh Haavodah)], as it is written (ibid. 19: 6): “it rejoices like a mighty man, running,” (Midrassh Tadshe, ch. 2). The “beth” of בֹּעַז is like the “mem” in (Bereshit 5:29) נֹחַ יְנַחֲמֵנוּ and in (Shmuel I 1:20) שְּׁמוּאֵל כִּי מֵה' שְׁאִלְתִּיו.

and he named the right one Yachin although the moon is smaller than the sun, i.e., that it shou ld help him like an established moon, but not like a diminishing moon. Said Shlomo, “If the Holy One, blessed be He, compares my kingdom to the sun and the moon, I too shall make an established and enduring thing, namely, large copper pillars.” Another explanation: Churam, who was one of the sons of Dan, made the pillars. He called one Yachin after his father Shimshon, about whom Scripture states (Jud. 16:29): “And Shimshon grasped the two pillars of the center, etc.” And Shlomo called the second one Boaz after his grandfather, Boaz. A similar instance is (Bereshit 31:47): “And Lavan called it Yegar Sahadutha.”
ten cubits from brim to brim Ten by ten in its center, circular around.
and a line of thirty cubits did encompass it round about Whatever has a circumference of three handbreadths has a diameter of one handbreadth.
and the height thereof was five cubits its depth.

And the likeness of oxen was beneath it And he cast the forms of the likeness of oxen from it to stand upon, and they were fastened to it, as is stated at the end of the verse: “The oxen were cast when it was cast.”

round about, encompassing it; ten cubits encompassing the sea It is not elucidated here what the thing that encompassed them was, but in Melachim I (7:24) it is written: “And under the brim were ornamental knobs encompassing it round about, for ten cubits, encompassing the sea round about.” Knobs are like those made for cups, round pomels (apple-shaped) knobs, for the sake of beauty, and beneath its brim and round about, they stood in the three lowest cubits, which were square, and the two round upper ones. And it is impossible to contain [that which Scripture says] (ibid. verse 26): “it contained two thousand bath,” which are the equivalent of one hundred fifty purifying pools, except in this matter, as is delineated in Erubin (13a). And it is impossible to say that the upper ones were square and the lower ones were round, because that which is written: “it was round all about,” refers to its brim, and that which Scripture states about these knobs, “ten cubits” on each side, but where it was round, it is impossible to say, “ten cubits around.”
two rows the knobs were cast when it was cast;
all were cast together, not that he attached the knobs after its casting, with nails or with glue, called soldure in Old French, soldering.

and all their hind parts were inward The hind parts of all these oxen were facing inward (to) their bottom; those in the north their hind parts were facing opposite those in the south, and those in the east opposite those in the west.
And its thickness was a handbreadth [i.e.] its bottom and its walls, but at its mouth it was thin, spread out and flattened.
like the work of the brim of a cup used for drinking, upon which is depicted a lily flower.

it contained three thousand It contained this amount, but in Melachim I (7:26) it is written: “It contained two thousand baths.” The heaped measure was a third, for a bath is three seah, as is said: (Yechezkel 45:11): “The ephah and the bath shall have one volume.” Thus you have six thousand seah. This equals a hundred and fifty purifying pools for four thousand seah equal a hundred mikvaoth. And we find also for the remaining two thousand seah fifty mikvaoth, and even if you divide the vessel according to the measure that the Rabbis computed, namely a cubit by a cubit by the height of three cubits for a mikvah, you will find the same: for the height of three cubits, which was square, and which was ten by ten from its brim to its brim, are a hundred mikvaoth, and for the height of two cubits, where it was round, ten by ten from its brim to its brim around equal fifty mikvaoth, because a square is a fourth more than a circle.
And he made ten lavers in addition to Moshe’s.
and he placed five on the right of Moshe’s laver.
and five on the left to wash with them This is the sanctification of the hands and feet.

the performance of the burnt offering they would rinse with them With the water of the laver they would rinse the innards of the burnt offering, and only the burnt offering, but not the peace offering, because it was eaten by the owners and throughout the city. The lavers were for sanctification and the sea for immersion.

And he made the ten golden candelabra according to their regulations Why is it stated in connection with the candelabra, “according to their regulations”? Because he informs us why he made ten candelabra, and everything he deduced from the Torah: the flowers, the knobs, the almond-shaped cups enumerated in the chapter were seventy, meaning that for each of the ten candelabra were seven lamps. (This is how my mother’s brother, my uncle, Rabbi Klonimos the son of Rabbi Yehudah explained it, and it is a midrash), and its seven lamps corresponded to the seven planets: Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars.
and placed them in the Heichal, five from the right of Moshe’s candelabrum.
and five from the left but they were all in the south.
from the left of the table in the north.
and he made a hundred golden basins with which to sprinkle the blood on the altar.
And he made the priests’ court This is known as the ְעֶזרַת הַכֹּהֲנִים.
and the large court This is the court of Bnei Yisrael.

from the right side eastward, opposite the south He distanced it from the east, from opposite the entrance to the south of the forecourt, because it is neither respectful nor fitting that they should immerse themselves opposite the entrance of the vestibule.
And Churam made the pots Copper pots, made to gather the ashes to put them into the pots.
and the two bowls and chapiters atop the pillars for the two pillars.
and the networks were two These are the chains mentioned above (3:16), and the proof that it is so is that neither here nor in Kings does he mention the chains anywhere.
to cover the two bowls of the chapiters to cover the hollow of the chapiters with chains, and those branches were like palm branches, as I explained (ad loc.).

And the four hundred pomegranates Above (ad loc.), he states: “and he made a hundred pomegranates.” How so? We must explain it in this manner: He surely made four hundred pomegranates, as is stated here, and where it is stated [that he made] a hundred, it means a hundred for each row, for there were four rows, as it is stated: “two rows of pomegranates to one network,” and so two rows of pomegranates to the other network, totaling four rows, and the pomegranates were strung within the networks, which were set and inserted to cover the two bowls of the chapiters.
And he made the bases But in Melachim I (7:27), it is written: “And he made the ten bases of copper.” The bases are the bases of the laver, and there their work is explained.

And the pots, and the shovels, and the forks Although we already mentioned it above, he repeats it again, to let us know that they were copper, and also to let us know about the forks, which were not mentioned above.

burnished - Heb. מָרוּק, similar to (Yirmiyahu 46:4): “polish (מִרְקוּ) the spears,”; (Vayikra 6: 21): “it shall be scoured (וּמרַק) and rinsed with water.” In Melachim I (7:45), it is written מְמרָט, like (Vayikra 13:40): “whose head will become bald (יִמָּרֵט),” and the Targum renders: fine copper.
in the thickness of the ground The Targum renders: clay, ardille in Old French.

between Sukkot and Zeredathah In Melachim I (7: 46) it says Tzartan. Zeredathah was the place of Yerovam, (11: 26): “And Yerovam the son of Nevat, an Efrati of Tzredah, whose mother’s name was Tzruah, a widow.” Since a corpse conveys ritual contamination in a tent, and a mezora likewise, and so it is with an idol, as we learned at the end of the third chapter of Abodah Zarah (Mishnah 8). “A widow” means that he widowed [isolated] Yisrael from its Elokim. “From Tzredah” means that he narrowed the Torah and did not broaden it; i.e., מִן הַצְרֵדָתָה, means הֵצַר דַּת אֱלֹהֵינוּ he narrowed the law of our Elokim. My uncle of blessed memory explained it to me in this manner.

And the candelabra and their lamps To remove [the false idea] from the hearts of those who explain that the lamps were made from the body of the candelabrum and attached to it, because it is written: “and the candelabra and their lamps.” Since Scripture mentions the lamps separately and not the remaining work of the candelabrum separately, namely the cups and the flowers, we deduce that the lamps were not attached, and since they were not attached to it, they appeared like a different work, and it was necessary to mention the lamps, but the other works, which were attached to it, he does not mention because they are called by the name of the candelabrum, and [the reason] he made ten candelabra, ten tables, ten lavers, the cherubim, and all that he made is explained in the Baraitha of Rabbi Pinchas the son of Yair (Midrash Tadshe, ch. 2).

And the flower Our Rabbis explained that this corresponds to the flower that Moshe added in the section, “Behaalothecha”: (Bamidbar 8:4) “to its rootstock, to its flower, etc.,” which is not mentioned in “Terumah.”
and the tongs were gold with which they would lift up the wick from the lamp containing oil.

it was fine gold Refined and purified gold, fin in Old French, refined, pure, and in Menahoth (29a) it is explained: out of all the gold that Shlomo had, out of the abundance of gold that entered the candelabrum to refine it and purify it and to fulfill the commandment of making a candelabrum of pure gold.
And the musical instruments - Heb. וְהַמְזַמְּרוֹת.
and the basins with which to sprinkle the blood on the altar.
and the spoons for th e spoons of frankincense (Vayikra 24:7).

and the censers with which to gather up the part of the ashes that is separated [from the rest and cast beside the altar, as in Vayikra 6:31, (and the rest of the ashes) to pick up from the altar, (ibid. 16:12): “And he shall take a full censer, etc.”

and Shlomo brought his father David’s hallowed things Whatever is mentioned in this verse—according to its simple meaning—refers to that which remained to him from the things that David hallowed, as is written above (Divrei Hayamim I 18:11): “Those also King David dedicated to Hashem, [along] with the silver and the gold that he took from all the nations, etc.,” and that which he left over he deposited into the treasuries of the House of Elokim. And [in] Midrash Aggadah (Pesikta Rabbathi 6:7), some sages say that [he did not use these articles for the building of the Temple] because he knew that it was destined to be destroyed, in order that the nations should not say, “Our deity is strong,” for it took revenge on this House, which was built from the loot and the spoils that David robbed from their heathen temples. Some say: So said Shlomo, “There was a famine during the days of David my father for three consecutive years, year after year, and he should have given away these hallowed things to sustain the poor of Yisrael with them.” I wish to bring support [to the view that Shlomo did not build the Temple with the spoils of the nations], for regarding all the devoted things that David dedicated, as is written above (ibid.), it is not stated that with this Shlomo made such and such a thing, as it is stated regarding the copper, as it is said (ibid. verse 8): “And from Tibhath and from Kun, cities of Hadadezer, David took huge quantities of copper, with which Shlomo made the copper sea, etc.,” but of the silver and gold, about which it is not stated that Shlomo made anything from it, it may be deduced that he did not make [anything from it]. Therefore, it is not written here any copper, but silver and gold. According to the simple interpretation, it seems to me that Scripture does not mention copper because copper is cheap, and it is not proper or fitting to bring it into the treasuries of the House of Elokim.

Then Shlomo assembled the elders of Yisrael He conducted [the matter] with the attribute of wisdom, in that he gathered the elders, and not the youths, [which was] better than David [had done,] who gathered even the youths, as it is written, “And David assembled all the leaders of Yisrael...Yerushalayim” (Divrei Hayamim I 28:1).
on the festival the festival of Sukkot.

and the Tent of Meeting that Moshe made, Shlomo hid it in the treasuries of the House of Elokim with the remaining vessels and the hallowed articles, because he did not need them, and our Sages (Tosefta of Sotah 13:1) said that they were hidden away.
all the sacred vessels that were in the Tent that David had given to the Ark.

the priests and the Leviyim brought them up. This refers back to the above, where Scripture says: “and the Leviyim bore the Ark,” and he explains: Who were those Leviyim that I mentioned to you above? The Levitic priests, for the priests are also of the sons of Levi, but they were not real Leviyim, and so it is written (Melachim I 8:3): “and the priests took up the Ark.” And the Leviyim also brought up the vessels and the Tent of Meeting according to their regulations.
And the cherubim were spreading their wings over the place of the Ark in the place where the Ark was standing Therefore -

and the cherubim covered over the Ark and over its staves from above above the Ark. So were the staves standing, and they extended so far out toward the east, that the Ark could stand exactly beneath the cherubim without the hindrance of the staves. Therefore, “and the cherubim covered over the Ark.” And they also covered part of the staves adjacent to the Ark, but not all of them, because they reached until the east. But you cannot explain that the cherubim covered the entire staves. And also, because of this—And they extended the staves so that the ends of the staves were seen from the Ark before the Dvir For if it were not so, but [if they were] the same; i.e., if they were extended with one measure one from the other, [i.e., the part of the staves extending eastward equaled the part extending westward]. The staves that Moshe made were still there, and they stood in the Holy of Holies of the Tent of Meeting, which was only ten [cubits], whereas this was twenty [cubits], and it reached from wall to wall. With the cherubim of Moshe, about which it is also written, “spreading and covering,” they did not have to move any part of the staves from their place, because the cherubim of Moshe were standing over the Ark on the Ark cover, but as for the cherubim mentioned here-Solomon made them standing on their feet on the ground, but nevertheless, those of Moshe were still attached to the Ark cover. This is how Rabbi Natan explained it, (but our Rabbi explained) that the priests wished to bring the Ark into the Dvir with its staves, but they were unable to do so, because the Cloud filled the House of Hashem, and they could not bring the cherubim up to the western wall. Therefore, they [the staves] protruded into the dividing curtain. To me, this poses a difficulty, however, because it is written (Melachim I 8:10f.): “And it came to pass when the priests came out, etc.,” and afterwards, “the glory of Hashem filled the House of Elokim (sic).” (Rabbi Yosef of blessed memory, however, explained) that it does not say וַיִּתְאָרְכוּ [in the reflexive conjugation], which would mean that they became elongated by themselves, but וַיַּאֲרִיכוּ [in the causative conjugation], which means that others elongated them, and he explained that the craftsmen elongated them to twenty cubits, and their two ends touched the eastern wall and their [other] two ends touched the western wall. It is, however, puzzling how they could spread out their wings and cover the Ark, which was ten cubits from them.

And it came to pass when the priests left the Holy He should have immediately written, “and the House became full of the cloud of the House of Hashem,” but he interrupted in between, and so in Melachim I (8:10): “And it came to pass, when the priests came out of the Holy, and the cloud filled the House of Hashem.”
for all the priests that were present had sanctified themselves for this thing.
not taking heed of the divisions The twenty-four of the Leviyim and the twenty-four of the priests, but all those present sanctified themselves.

And the trumpeters, etc. were as one The meaning is: And they were united - all the trumpeters together. Now for what purpose were they united? To make one sound together to praise and to thank Hashem.

Then Shlomo said Since the House is full of smoke, I now know that the Shechinah is resting in the thick darkness therein, for so is His wont, as it is written (Shemot 20:18): “and Moshe drew near to the thick darkness wherein Elokim appeared.” [Therefore, I deduce that] He surely wishes to stay therein, and in Sifre it is explained: Then Shlomo said - when he saw the cloud, he said, “Now I see that the Shechinah rests in the House that I have built, for He promised to come and dwell therein out of the midst of the cloud and the thick darkness.” Now where did He say this? (Vayikra 16:2): “for in the cloud I shall appear on the Ark cover.”
a House to dwell in - Heb. בֵית זְבֻל a dwelling.
for You to dwell in forever For since it was selected, the Shechinah did not rest elsewhere, and the high places were prohibited.
and blessed all the congregation of Yisrael the blessing stated at the end of the episode.
Who spoke with His mouth that He would give him a son who would build Him a House.
has fulfilled He fulfilled His good word.
Since the day that I brought forth For this too You spoke to my father.
And I chose Yerushalayim This refers to “I chose no city.”
and I chose David This refers back to “neither did I choose a man.”
you did well that it was in your heart i.e., I too choose the House that you thought to build, where My name shall dwell, as is stated above.

and he spread forth his hands Scripture should have said the following: “and he spread forth his hands toward heaven, and he said, etc.,” but it interrupted in between to inform [us] on what he stood, and so in Melachim I (8:22f.): “and he spread forth his hands towards heaven, and he said.”
For Shlomo had made This refers back to “opposite all the congregation of Yisrael,” i.e., how was he higher than all of them to make his words heard?

and he stood on it And now, all Yisrael could see him, and since he interrupted the topic, he had to repeat, “opposite all the congregation of Yisrael,” and so, “and he spread forth his hands toward heaven.”

there is no Elokim like You insofar as You keep the covenant and the kindness that You decree from heaven to give to those who love You. You hide and conceal the covenant and the kindness to fulfill Your promise on earth.
who walk before You as my father David walked, and this is [the meaning of] For You have kept for Your servant David with an expression referring to the realization of a promise.

But will Elokim indeed dwell with man on the earth? This is an expression of wonder. Is it possible for man to believe that Elokim will dwell on the earth? For the heaven and the heaven of the heaven, etc. However, because of the kindness that You bestowed upon my father, David, You contracted Your Shechinah.
much less this House that I have built So why did I build it? To pray before Elokim and so that He should turn to our prayers.

to the cry - Heb. הָרִנָּה. This is a cry, like (Melachim I 22:36): “A cry (הָרִנָּה) passed through the camp.” Perforce, concerning the cry of any man who flees in distress, he will not pray but express his cry in secret. This is the sequence of the verses, and the conclusion of the topic proves it, for he says, “You shall hear from Your abode.” You have thus learned that he built it only with this intention to bring down the Shechinah therein, in order that He dwell on the earth, to hear “from Your abode” the prayer that they will pray therein.
That Your eyes may be open, etc. whenever they pray to You.

If a man sins This verse refers to all Yisrael; whoever exacts an oath from his neighbor - if he is adjuring him legitimately, and the one swearing is swearing falsely, You shall hear from heaven. If, on the other hand, justice is on the side of the one who swears, for the litigant exacts an oath from him for naught, even the one who exacts the oath is called wicked.

and to justify the righteous not to punish him for the oath, for he swore in truth. Tosefta of Sotah (1: 3) explains [this verse as referring to the rite of the sotah, the married woman accused of adultery Bamidbar 5:11-30)]: If a man sins by being intimate with a married woman. and an oath be exacted of him and an oath makes him guilty, for just as the water tests her, so does the water test him. before Your altar - as it is written (Bamidbar 5:18): “And the priest shall have the woman stand [before the Lord].”
to bring his way upon his head - as it is written (ibid. verse 27): “her belly will swell and her thigh will fall away.”
and to justify the righteous - (ibid. verse 28): “and she will be blessed with offspring.”
And if Your people...is struck down not because You have no power, but because they will sin against You.

and confess - Heb. וְהוֹדוּ. The meaning is: and they will confess their iniquity, and the latter verse proves this (verse 26): “and confess to Your name and repent of their sin, so that You may answer them.”
and bring them back to the land For when they fall and are struck down before their enemies, they [their enemies] will seize what they can and will bring them into captivity to another land.
When heaven is shut up as it is written (Devarim 11:17): “and He will shut up the heaven, and there will be no rain.”

for You will teach them the good way as You did when there was a famine in David’s time for three years (Shmuel II 21:1), and You taught them and said to them, “(It is) for Shaul and (also) for his bloody house.” Likewise, so shall You teach them which sin causes them [their distress], for what reason the heaven was shut up.

whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness (there be) The meaning is: I have mentioned to You pestilence, blast and mildew, being struck down [in battle], and lack of rainfall, and what else can I include, but whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness there may be, and he pray and spread forth his hands toward this House, and this is what it says.
Any prayer, any supplication that he will pray and supplicate about, concerning any of these matters.
every man shall know his plague i.e., if he pray about his affliction or about his sickness to remove it from him.

and forgive and give to each man according to his ways, etc. to the wicked according to his wickedness and to the righteous according to his righteousness. For if He does not repay the wicked according to his wickedness, he will speak insolently toward Heaven, and he will say, “There is no Elokim.” Then [the thoughts of] his heart will be known, and there will be a profanation of the Name [of Hashem]. Likewise shall You do to the righteous according to his righteousness, which You shall do for him when he prays to You.
That they may fear You and the wicked will repent of his way; therefore, I pray to give each man according to his ways.

and You shall do whatever the stranger calls upon You Concerning a Yisraeli, I pray to give him according to his ways, but concerning a heathen, according to all the stranger calls upon You, because Bnei Yisrael recognize the Holy One, blessed be He, and they know that He has the ability to do, and if his prayer is not heard, he assigns the cause to himself, to his sins, and he searches his deeds, but the heathen will complain of injustice and say, “I heard His fame throughout the world, and I toiled on many roads until I came and prayed in this place, and I did not find reality in Him any more than the other deities.” Therefore, You shall do whatever the stranger calls upon You.
toward the city With their faces toward Yerushalayim.
and maintain their cause their revenge from their enemies. Another meaning is: their necessities. A similar instance is (Melachim I 8:59): “that He sustain the cause of His servant.”

that I built for Your name The meaning is: this House, which I built in order to aggrandize Your name, for when You accept their prayer, they will pray to You in this House; wherever they are, they will turn to this, Your House.
You shall hear, etc. And through this, Your name will be aggrandized in the world.
And now, arise, O Hashem so as not to have to move as until now, from Shiloh to Nov and from Nov to Givon.
You and the Ark of Your might that it will no longer move from now on.

Your might Because of the following it is called “Your might”: because it performed wonders and mighty deeds among the Plishtim. And so it is written above (Divrei Hayamim I 16:8-36): “Give thanks to Hashem,” “Search for Hashem and His might.” Our Sages stated further in Tractate Abodah Zarah 24b (Shmuel I 6:12): “And the cows sang.” What song did they recite? They said, (Tehillim 98:1) “His right hand and His holy arm have gained Him the victory.”
shall be attired with salvation because they will not wander from place to place, like (Yeshayahu 11:5): “And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins.”
and Your pious ones shall rejoice with the goodness with the abundance of goodness and tithes that will be given to the Leviyim as reward for guarding the Ark and singing before it.
do not turn back the face of Your anointed one by not treating me with goodness, and if not for my sake, do it for Your sake.
And the priests...on their watches as David had divided them into twenty-four watches, for each watch to serve its week, and the Leviyim likewise on their twenty-four watches
to give thanks with musical instruments, for they recited (Tehillim 136): “Give thanks to Hashem for He is good, for His loving kindness is eternal.”
with David’s praise The musical instruments with which they recited David’s praise and the thanksgivings were in the Leviyim’s hands.

and the priests were sounding the trumpets opposite them For it was incumbent upon them to play music with the trumpets, as it is said (Bamidbar 10: 8): “And the sons of Aharon, the priests, shall blow [with the trumpets].”

And Shlomo consecrated the interior of the court Our Sages differ in this matter (Zeb. 59): Rabbi Yehudah says: He consecrated the floor of the forecourt with the sanctity of the altar to burn offerings on the floor, because the copper altar was too small to contain [the offerings], because they brought many sacrifices. Rabbi Yosei said to him: Was it not already stated (1:6): “And he offered up on it a thousand burnt offerings” on the altar that Moshe had made? When you compute the number of cubits and the number of burnt offerings, you will find that this one of stones was larger than that of Moshe, for on Moshe’s altar, the place of its pyre was a cubit by a cubit, whereas on Shlomo’s, the place of its pyre was twenty-four by twenty-four. The result is that Shlomo’s [altar] was 576 times as large as that of Moshe. If so, what is the meaning of (Melachim I 8:64): “the king consecrated the interior of the court”? That he set the stone altar into it, fastened to the floor.
could not contain He is talking about Moshe’s [altar], like a person who says, “So and so is a dwarf and is disqualified from performing the sacrificial service.”
from the entrance of Chamat which is in the north of the land of Yisrael.
to the brook of Mitzrayim which is opposite it, as is delineated in אֵלֶּה מַסְעֵי (ibid. verse 5).

And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he dismissed the people which was the ninth [day] of the inauguration of the Temple, but in Melachim I (8:66) it is written: “On the eighth day,” which was the twenty-second of the month. The meaning is: On the eighth day he gave them permission to leave after the Feast, and on the morrow, when the Feast was over, they all went [home] together. Another meaning: On the eighth day he gave them permission and dismissed those who lived within the Sabbath limits and whoever wished to travel and go on that day in that limit, and on the following day, he dismissed the entire populace. In Genesis Rabbah (35:3) it is explained that they took his leave but waited there one more day and then they repeated [this procedure] and took leave again a second time; therefore it is said: “on the twenty-third day of the month.”

rejoicing and delighted of heart, etc. for David, for Shlomo For that which He spoke with His mouth above (Divrei Hayamim I 28:6): “Your son Shlomo - he shall build My House,” He fulfilled with His hand, for He gave him a son sitting on his throne, who built a House in the name of Hashem. And in Genesis Rabbah it is explained: Said Rabbi Levi: It is written: “for the inauguration of, etc.” “Rejoicing” refers to “that Hashem had wrought for David,” viz. that He fulfilled that which He had vowed to Shlomo, that He chose him from all his brothers because he was wise.

and for Yisrael His people it is written in Melachim I (8:56): “there has not failed one word, etc.” Another explanation: “and for Yisrael His people” - they had a ruler, so that they dwelt safely and tranquilly, as it is written (ibid. 5:5): “And Yehudah and Yisrael dwelt, etc.”
And Hashem appeared to Shlomo at night in a vision of the night.

I have heard your prayer With the wording that Shlomo used, “And You shall hear.” The Holy One, blessed be He, answered him: “I have heard your prayer.” He prayed, (above 6:26): “When heaven is closed up.” And the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, “If I close up.” He prayed concerning famine and locusts, and the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, “if I command locusts.” He prayed concerning pestilence, and the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, “or if I send pestilence upon My people.
and My people... humble themselves” by praying and seeking My presence and repenting of their evil ways. Hence we have three [responses] corresponding to three [entreaties].
If I shut up... if I command...or if I send corresponding to three prayers, “I shall hear...and forgive their sin, and heal their land.”
and My eyes and heart will be Jonathan renders (Melachim I 9:3): “and My presence will rest there if My will is performed there at all times.” My eyes will be there if My heart and My will are there.

I shall cast from before Me according to the condition between Me and you, viz. (Vayikra 26: 14): “But if you do not heed Me.” What does it say there? (verse 31): “And I shall make your sanctuaries desolate.”
and I shall make it a proverb as people compose a proverb about someone who was befallen by misfortune.

and a byword - Heb. וְלִשְׁנִינָה, like (Devarim 6:7): וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ, “and you shall teach them.” [It is] an expression of recounting misfortunes. Similarly, the Targum of (Bereshit 37:10) וַיְסַפֵּר “And he told,” is וְאִשְׁתָּעֵי, and [the Targum of] וְלִשְׁנִינָה is וּלְשׁוּעֵי.

every passerby will be astounded i.e., The Temple will be destroyed, and every passerby will then be astounded (יִשֹּׁם), like (Iyov 18:20): “Concerning his day - the later people shall be astonished (נָשַׁמּוּ).”
Why has Hashem done בַּמֶּה, like (Devarim 29:23): “Why (עַל מֶה) has Hashem done thus,” and so it is written in Melachim I (9:9).

Now it came to pass at the end of twenty years The meaning is: at the end of twenty years that the entire construction had been completed: that of the House of Hashem seven years and that of his palace thirteen years, as it is written in Melachim I (6:38, 7:1).

And he built Tadmor in the desert In Melachim I (9:18) it [the name] is written “Tamar,” but read, “Tadmor.” This accounts for that which we learned in Tractate Jebamoth (16a): We may not accept proselytes from the Tarmodites; and in Genesis Rabbah (56:11), in the portion dealing with the binding [of Yitzchak] it is explained that they aided Yisrael’s enemies, and because they changed themselves and became worse, the word תָּמָר is used in Kings, an expression of exchange (תְּמוּרָה), for they should have repaid Yisrael for the kindness that Shlomo bestowed upon them, for he built the city of Tadmor for them. Because of Shlomo, it is not written here “Tamar,” but “Tadmor,” i.e., an important city, in deference to Shlomo’s honor, for it is no honor to Shlomo to say here that he built a city which rebelled against him and sinned against him. Therefore, it is written, “Tadmor,” and not “Tamar.”
fortified cities Because they stood on the border, they needed to be fortified.

for his work [i.e.] for the work of his building. Why? All the proselytes were [employed] to do his work, but not the men of Yisrael, because Bnei Yisrael served as soldiers and men of war and the officers of his chariots and his horsemen.

two hundred fifty And in Melachim I (9:23): “five hundred fifty,” but [in fact], these two are identical, for there Scripture deducts three hundred and then repeats and counts them again, for there it is written (5:30): “Besides Shlomo’s chief officers, etc....three thousand and three hundred, who bore rule,” and here it is written above (2:1): “three thousand six hundred.” We find that what is missing in one verse is added in the other verse. Scripture separates them because the three hundred extra were proselytes, and they were appointed over those three thousand three hundred who ruled over the seventy thousand who bore burdens and the eighty thousand hewers in the mountains (Melachim I 5:29), and these two hundred fifty were Bnei Yisrael, appointed over those three hundred proselytes.
Shlomo brought up from the City of David That is Tziyon, for he let her dwell in the City of David when he married her, and she was there until he completed building his palace.
because they are holy The entire city and all the houses.

since the Ark of Hashem came to them because the Ark of Hashem had come to them. [The word] בָּאָה is a feminine expression, similar to (Shmuel I 4:17): “and the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem (sic) was taken (נִלְקְחָה).”

on the altar of Hashem This was the copper altar that Shlomo built. Some explain that this was the copper altar that Shlomo made instead of the copper altar that Moshe built, but this is astounding, because it is written (Melachim II 16:15): “and the burnt offerings of the entire people of the land, etc. and the blood of every burnt offering, etc. shall be for me to visit,” i.e., the copper altar, which was there heretofore, shall be for me to visit. This proves that Moshe’s copper altar was still there.
until this day [from] the founding of the House of the Lord From the day of its founding until its completion.
to test Shlomo whether that which she had heard about his wisdom was true, and she came to test him.
with riddles - Heb. בְחִידוֹת like (Jud. 14:12): “Let me ask you a riddle (אָחוּדָה נָא לָכֶם חִידָה),” [in the story] of Shimshon.

and nothing was hidden Since she saw that he told her everything, and nothing that she asked him was hidden, she admitted that the report she had heard was true. In the Targum (Sheni) of Megillath Esther (1:2), some of the riddles that she asked him are written.
And the food of his table fowl (Melachim I 5:3) and kinds of delicacies that were served on his table in abundance.

and the seating of his servants That each one recognized his place when they were seated at the table, and of those who constantly saw the king’s face, no one was allowed to sit in his neighbor’s place all the days of his life.
and the station of his attendants Each one would retain his station and his position, and he would not change it the next day.
and their attire The attire that they would wear tomorrow was not the same as, the attire that they wore today.
and his cupbearers most of his cupbearers.
and his ascent the stairway by which he ascended from his palace to the Temple.

and she was breathless because she thought that there was no wisdom in any of the kingdoms but in her own country and like that of her wise men, because her country was in the east; they were wise because they were stargazers, as is stated in the first chapter of Tractate Rosh Hashanah, for Eretz Yisrael is west of Bavel, and that is what is written (Melachim I 5:10): “And Shlomo’s wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the children of the east,” for they were in the east, as it is written (Bereshit 11: 2): “And it came to pass as they migrated from the east.” (Melachim I 5:10) “And all the wisdom of Mitzrayim,” for they were sorcerers, necromancers, and astrologers, and he was wise in divination (טַיִיר). So it is written in Pesikta (d’Rav Kahana p. 33b). The word (טַיִיר) is Arabic, and in Leviticus Rabbah (32:2), in the chapter dealing with the son of the Mitzri (24:10): (Kohelet 10:20): “for a bird of the air shall carry the voice.” This is the raven and refers to the art of bird divination (טוּיאַרִי).
half of your abundant [wisdom] The many wisdoms.

algom wood In Pesikta it is explained: One verse (Melachim I 10:11) says אַלְמֻגִּים, and one verse says אַלְגּוּמִּים. The truth is that its name is אַלְגּוּמִּים, but it is called אַלְמֻגִּים because it melted and bent because of its softness, (like cups, which bend because of their value.)

a path מְסִלּוֹת, stairs. In Melachim I (10:12) it is written מִסְעָד, [a support] after the manner that they make for those who ascend by way of elevated places and stairs. Some say that מִסְעָד and מְסִילָה are one and the same.

and harps and psalteries for the singers Some say (Jonathan and Rashi to Kings) for the Leviyim who sing with musical instruments, and Rabbi Eliezer explained it to mean: for the singers who stroll before the king. A similar case is (Melachim I 5:12): “and his songs were a thousand and five.” These were secular songs that he composed to sing before him, and that is what is meant (below 35:25): “And Yirmiyahu lamented over Yoshiyahu, and all the male singers and the female singers recited in their lamentations, etc.”

aside from that which she brought This is written here in deference to the honor of the kings of Yehudah; it means that she gave him more than he gave her, and in Melachim I (10:13) it is written: “aside from that which he gave her according to King [Shlomo’s] ability.” [He gave her] things that were common in the land of Yisrael, but were not common in her country.
Aside from that which the guides - Heb. הַתָּרִים. They were afraid to pass from province to province or from kingdom to kingdom without a guide, and they would give him the guide’s fee.
and the merchants would bring They would bring him [gold] on a pretext in order to see his wisdom.
two hundred shields צִנָּה which encompasses the person from his three sides, as is written (Tehillim 5: 13): “As a shield You encompass him with favor” (כַּצִּנָּה).
malleable gold gold that is soft and easily flattened out. It had great value because it could be spun like a thread.
six hundred gold pieces Six hundred zehubim, the equivalent of six manehs, for the zahab is the dinar.

the forest of Levanon Shlomo built a huge house in Yerushalayim, as is proven further, and Shishak took all those shields (below 12:9), and he made them (sic) from an abundance of the large trees of Levanon, as it is written in Melachim I (7:2): “And he built the house of the forest of Levanon, etc. on four rows, etc.,” and there he deposited those shields, and that is what is written (Yeshayahu 22:8): “and you looked on that day to the weapons of the house of the forest.”
ivory throne the ivory of elephants.
And there were six steps to the throne steps by which to ascend.
with armrests on either side by the place of the seat like rods from corner to corner, from the right and from the left, upon which to support his arms.

and two lions were standing beside the armrests [The lions were made] of gold, and the entire form of the throne and the forms of the beasts that were in the throne are depicted in the Targum of the Scroll of Esther (1:2).
ivory the tusks of elephants and the elephants themselves.
and apes In German, meerkats, long- tailed monkeys.
and peacocks - Heb. וְתוּכִּיִּים.
Now King Shlomo transcended, etc. To fulfill that which He said to him, (Melachim I 3:13): “And I have also given you that which you have not asked, etc. and honor.”
And all the kings of the earth, etc. To fulfill that which He said to him, (ibid. verse 12): “Behold I have given you a wise and understanding heart; so that there was none like you before you.”

And each one would bring his gift as a pretext because they were [really] coming to hear [his wisdom], since it is disrespectful to come before a king empty-handed, similar to (Devarim 16:16): “and he shall not appear before Hashem empty-handed.”
weapons - Heb. נֶשֶׁק.

and he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Yerushalayim. some of them. He transgressed [the negative commandment of] (Devarim 17:17): “Only he shall not multiply horses to himself.”
in the words of Natan the prophet (Shmuel II 12:25): “And He sent by the hand of Natan the prophet, and he called his name Yedidyah for Hashem’s sake.”
and in the prophecy of Achiyah the Shiloni (Melachim I 11:31) who rent the kingdom from him and gave it to Yerovam.
over all Yisrael forty years unlike David, who reigned seven years in Chevron and thirty-three years in Yerushalayim.

for all Yisrael had come to Shechem to make him king In Shechem, which was Yerovam’s place, which was in the territory of Efraim. And Yerovam was an Ephrathite, and all this was brought about by the Holy One, blessed be He, to fulfill His word, (Melachim I 11:11): “I will surely tear the kingdom.”
And it was when... heard The meaning is: And it was when he heard - prior to this, when they came to make him [Rechavam] king in Shechem, when he [Yerovam] was still in Mitzrayim.

And they sent and called him, and...came All this was to let us know the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, that even Yerovam himself came to make Rechavam king, but the Holy One, blessed be He, reversed his words [i.e., Yerovam’s intention,] until Yerovam reigned.

Your father made our yoke hard because he was a man who toiled at work, and he made it incumbent upon us to sustain his laborers with the tax, as it is written in Melachim I (5:27): “And King Shlomo raised a levy, etc.”

How do you advise - Heb. נוֹעָצִים, [in the passive voice], like יוֹעֲצִים [in the active voice], and so he says from יוֹדְעִים, נוֹדָעִים. יוֹעֲצִים means the future, and נוֹעָצִים means that which they already counseled.
My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins My little finger is larger than my father’s loins; i.e., I am stronger than he.
burdened - Heb. הֶעֱמִיס, loaded, like (Bereshit 44:13): “and each man loaded (וַיַַַַַּעֲמס) his donkey.”
with scorpions Brimmen in German, which sting like scorpions.

because it was brought about, etc. so that Hashem Hashem might establish His word as is delineated in Melachim I (11:31–37), to remove from him the ten tribes and to give them to Yerovam, and this is the meaning of (Bereshit 49:10): “The scepter will not depart from Yehudah” [meaning that] he will not be banished from his kingdom, “until he comes to Shiloh,” meaning until Yehudah comes to Shiloh to crown Rechavam there, and there “peoples will gather to him” to crown him, and there the kingdom was divided, and the reign over the ten tribes was lost. Now Shechem is a small city adjacent to Shiloh, as it is written at the end of Shoftim (21:19): “Behold, there is a sacrifice before Hashem in Shiloh from time to time, etc. on the east side of the highway that goes up from Beth-El to Shechem,” and it is written in Yirmiyahu (41:5): “from Shechem (and) from Shiloh,” and in honor of the Tabernacle of Shiloh, they would gather in Shechem, which was fit for the people to assemble in, and it adjoined Shiloh. And when they would assemble in Shechem, the scepter would depart from Yehudah, for there the kingdom was divided.
Each man to your homes, O Yisrael This refers back to, “What share do we have in David?” Why should we leave our homes and follow him? Not so, but all Yisrael, return each man to his home.

Now see your house, David This refers back to, “And no heritage in Yishai’s son,” i.e., we have no heritage in him, but in the Temple in Yerushalayim, where we sacrifice and appear on the three Pilgrimage Festivals.
see your house, David We do not need it to go there. Let it be yours alone. (But all this does not appeal to me) but, “See your house, David we have no desire either in you or in your Temple.”
Hadoram He is identical with Adoniram (Melachim I 4:6), for during Shlomo’s time, he enjoyed great eminence, but in Rechavam’s time his greatness was humbled. Therefore, he was called Hadoram.

and the Children of Yisrael pelted him with stones and because Rechavam did not know the cause of the rebellion in which they turned away from him, he was slain when he requested the levy that Shlomo had levied upon them.

And Bnei Yisrael rebelled against the house of David - Heb. וַיִפְשְׁעוּ, an expression of rebellion. Examples are (Melachim II 1:1): “Moav rebelled (וַיִפְשַׁע) against Yisrael”; (Mishlei 18:19): “A rebellious (נִפְשַׁע) brother”; (below 27:19): “then Livnah rebelled (תִּפְשַׁע).”

and he assembled the house of Yehudah and Binyamin who were together on the border. Yerushalayim belonged to both of them, and the Temple was built on their common border. In the section dealing with boundaries in Yehoshua, it explains how their border was shared. Our Rabbis also said (Yoma 12a, Meg. 26a, Zeb. 53b): A strip protruded from the territory of Binyamin and entered the territory of Yehudah, upon which the altar was built. Therefore, they were inseparable, and they are also mentioned close to one another.
with your brothers Are they not your brothers, the sons of one man?

and he built cities for fortification - Heb. לְמָצוֹר. He built small cities and surrounded them with water for strength, and this is [called] מָצוֹר as it is written in Yeshayahu (37:25): “I dug and drank water, and I dried up with the soles of my feet all rivers of fortification (מַָצוֹר).” And this was now necessary because Yisrael rebelled against him.
leaders chiefs and officers to guard the towns and the large cities.
and storehouses of food, oil, and wine in order to have food prepared for them should the house of Yisrael march upon them to besiege them.
For the Leviyim had abandoned their open land that was in the entire land of the ten tribes.
because Yerovam...had coerced them to abandon He coerced them to abandon serving and ministering to Hashem.
priests for the high places i.e., Why did Yerovam coerce them to abandon [their positions]? Because he stationed pagan priests for the satyrs.
And after them [i.e., after] the Leviyim and the priests.

Avihayil the daughter of Eliav Like: and Avihayil, similar to (Yirmiyahu 11:19): “And I was like a lamb and a bull (כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף).” The following was the reason that Shmuel the seer erred when Yishai passed Eliav before Shmuel, and he [Shmuel] said, (Shmuel I 16:6): “Surely before Hashem is His anointed.” This is the one about whom the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to say, “Arise, anoint him, for this is he.” But Shmuel erred about him, for he saw Eliav’s daughter as Rechavam’s wife, the queen, and because of the following matter, Shmuel was punished: When Shaul asked him, (ibid. 9: 18) “Which is the house of the seer?” Shmuel replied, “I am the seer,” in which case he did not answer him with humility, saying, “What do you wish.” [Therefore,] the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, “By your life, you are destined to see, and you will not know what you see,” for he erred concerning Eliav and his daughter the queen.
as a leader among his brothers in order to make him king.
and he dispersed He scattered his sons to all the lands of Yehudah. A similar expression is (Divrei Hayamim I 4:38): “And their fathers’ houses spread (פָּרְצוּ) exceedingly.”

They have humbled themselves; I shall not destroy them A similar instance is found below (14: 6): “The land is still before us for we have sought, etc. we have sought.” So is the custom of the Scriptures, that when it interrupts in the middle, it repeats the word. An example is (Bamidbar 10:32): “And it will be, if you go with us, it will be that the good, etc.”
For they will be his slaves [i.e., slaves] of Shishak and the other nations, as is explained.

and they will know My service When they repent, no ruler of the kings of the nations will be over them, but when you abandon My Law, you will experience servitude to the kings of the lands, and you will serve them.

and he entrusted them in the hands of the chiefs of the runners He took them from the house of the forest of Levanon and entrusted them to the chiefs of the runners and afterwards they returned them to the chamber of the runners The room of the runners, i.e., to their place. Another explanation I heard from my mentor is that because he was afraid of the king of Mitzrayim and the king of Yisrael, they would carry them [the shields] before him.

And when he humbled himself, Hashem’s wrath returned from him He should have stated this above immediately when he said, “And Shishak... marched,” but he interrupted in between because he had to mention, “And...made instead of them shields of copper.”

And King Rechavam strengthened himself in Yerushalayim And he explains why, because when he was first made king, he was forty-one years old; therefore, he had the strength and the power to strengthen himself. He was a year old when David died, for Shlomo reigned forty years, and Shlomo had not yet reigned when Rechavam was born. We find that Rechavam was forty-one years old when he reigned.

the city that Hashem had chosen wherein to place His name, out of all the tribes of Yisrael but they deteriorated in their deeds, as it is written: “And he did that which was evil, for he did not set his heart to seek Hashem,” and they caused the Shechinah to leave them, and it was as if they were complaining and demonstrating about that.

in the words of Shmayah the prophet Every prophet would write his book, containing that which he prophesied, and this is the Shmayah who was mentioned above (11:2, 12:5). And the verse written further (13:22), “And the rest of the deeds of Aviyah and his ways and his words are written in the midrash of the prophet Ido,” proves this, [that each prophet wrote a book of his prophecies, and] his [Ido’s] book was called midrash.

Three years he reigned in Yerushalayim and no more, as is proven in Melachim I (15:9): “And in the twentieth year of Yerovam, king of Yisrael, Asa reigned over Yehudah.” We find that he did not reign even three whole years.

Michayhu the daughter of Uriel And above (11:20), he calls her by a different name, Ma'achah the daughter of Avshalom, and in Melachim I (15:10), it is likewise written “Ma'achah the daughter of Avshalom.” Michayhu the daughter of Uriel was her [real] name, and here he calls her thus because this is the genealogical record of Yehudah. In Kings, which is the book of the kings of Yisrael and Yehudah, he calls her by her nickname, Ma'achah the daughter of Avshalom. Now, for this reason, they nicknamed her Ma'achah, rather than call her by her real name, Michayhu, (and the name of her father was Uriel Avishalom). She was called by the name of her daughter-in-law, who was a valiant woman, a heroic woman, as it is written (below 15:16): “And also Ma'achah the mother of King Asa he removed from being queen,” and in honor of her daughter-in-law, they called the mother-in-law by the daughter-in-law’s name. So it is explained in Yerushalmi (unknown). Now this tradition is in the name of Rabbi Eliezer, and he told me this in the name of his father, and so I found in his father’s commentary: Wherever a “vav” is added to the name of a woman, this is to her praise, like Atalyahu (below 22: 12): “and Atalyahu reigned over the land,” for she was a valiant woman; similarly Jecaliah (ibid. 26:3) and Jecaliahu (Melachim II 15:2), because she was a heroic woman, for Amatzyahu her husband fled to Lachish and was there fifteen years until he died, and she judged the people all those fifteen years, and later, when he died, they crowned his son Uziyahu after him at the age of sixteen.
And Aviyah arose For Aviyah went to war against Yerovam in Yerovam’s territory on Mount Efraim.
a covenant of salt with endurance and permanence. And now -
Yerovam, etc. the servant of Shlomo the son of David, arose, etc. and a great stigma is attached to this.
And there gathered to him worthless wicked.
and they overwhelmed Rechavam the son of Shlomo and Rechavam was young and soft-hearted and since they found in him humility and soft- heartedness, they overwhelmed him.
young - Heb. נַעַר. Although he was forty-one years old when he reigned, he is called a youth (נַעַר), as I explained above (Divrei Hayamim I 22:5) in regards to Shlomo.
like the peoples of the lands Whoever wishes to come and be initiated to be a priest to a golden calf, shall bring a young bull and seven rams, and be accepted.
to initiate himself - Heb. לְמַלֵּא יָדוֹ. To differentiate between impure and pure, similar to (Shemot 29:29): “to be anointed and initiated (וּלְמַלֵּא בָם אֶת יָדָם) through them.”
engage in the work i.e., in their work; this one to sing, and that one to guard the gates, every man to his work, as David prepared it.
And Yerovam could muster no more strength, etc., and Hashem smote him i.e., Yerovam.
and he died He did not die immediately, but continuously deteriorated because of the wars, and in Genesis Rabbah (65:20), it is explained that Hashem smote Aviyah.
And he commanded Yehudah to seek unlike the Ten Tribes, who sought other, new Gods, which came up of late, and did not seek the Elokim of their fathers.

as long as the land is before us As long as the kingdom is established before us, so that if we need them, they will be a refuge for us. And all this happened in the ten years about which it is written (above 13:23): “in his time the land was tranquil.” But after those ten years, there was a war between him and Basha all their lives, for in the third year of Asa, Basha reigned, and seven years there was peace between them, and so it is proven here as well (verse 5): “and there was no war with him in these years.” But in the other years there was war with him, and below (15:19) it is written: “And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.” We can, however, explain that the war that he had with the Kushim was not until the thirty-fifth year of his reign, but this is difficult to me, for it is written below (16:1): “In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Basha...advanced,” until (verse 9): “you have dealt foolishly concerning this, for from now on there will be wars with you.” It appears from here that prior to this, he did not have wars, and he lived after that only five years, and in Melachim I 15:32, it is written: “And there was war between Asa and Basha, etc. all their lives.” In Seder Olam (ch. 16) it is explained clearly.
for we sought Hashem our Elokim; we sought [Him] Since we sought Him, He gave us peace from round about.
So they built cities.
and prospered And a similar instance is (above 12:7): “And when Hashem saw that they had humbled themselves, etc.”

it makes no difference to You to aid i.e., even though we are few and they are as numerous as the sand by the sea, and we have no strength before them, You can help both the great and the powerless; it is known that You have strength to aid; therefore, help us, O Hashem our Elokim, for we have relied on You.

let no man rule against You Let not our enemies - man - have human strength to rule (עִמְּךָ) with You, i.e., against You, to be victorious, so that they should not say, “We have defeated their Elokim.” Another explanation from the Rabbi: Let not the weak one (אֱנוֹשׁ) be held back (יַעְצר), for we are weak, deprived of strength, keeping us back (עוֹצְרֵי יָד) from defeating them. And an example is (Devarim 11:17): “and He will hold back (וְעָצַר) the heaven”; (Bereshit 20:18): “For Hashem had held back (וְעָצר עָצַר),” and like (Jud. 13:16): “If you take me in (תַּעְצְרֵנִי).”
Now there were many days for Yisrael without a true Elokim until you came.
and without an instructing priest Since no one asks them words of Torah, the priests will not instruct you.

And they returned to Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, when they were in distress He means to say that now, when they were beset with troubles, they beseeched Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, and they sought Him; therefore, He was found by them, and He saved you (sic) wherever you went.

And in those times in those numerous days for Yisrael, [when they were] without a true Elokim there was no peace for anyone going or coming, etc. Concerning Rechavam it is written (above 12: 2): “Shishak, the king of Mitzrayim, marched against Yerushalayim, for they had betrayed Hashem.” Aviyah also experienced many turmoils.
And nation was crushed by nation - Heb. וְכֻתְּתוּ. Another instance of this is (Bamidbar 14:45): “and they struck them and crushed them (וַיַּכְּתוּם).”
But you be strong to seek Elokim.

And they sacrificed to Hashem on that day of the plunder they brought The meaning is: And the plunder that they brought, they sacrificed seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep which they had captured, and from that they brought, as above: (14:14): “And they also smote the tents of the livestock, and they captured many sheep. etc.” Another possible explanation is: “And they sacrificed to Hashem on that day” - when they were victorious and came in peace to Yerushalayim. “from the plunder they brought” - from the plunder that they had brought, i.e., seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep.

And also Ma'achah, King Asa’s mother he deposed from [being] the queen because she had made a frightful image for an asherah to gratify her lust. [מִפְלֶצֶת means] מַפְלֵא לֵצוּתָא. It carried lasciviousness to an extreme. She made herself a phallus for the image, and would copulate with it.

The high places, however, were not removed private high places, upon which they had become accustomed to sacrificing to Heaven from the time that Shiloh was destroyed until the Temple was built. [Those who worshipped there] were punishable by כָּרֵת, premature death.

And there was no war, etc. We learned in Seder Olam (ch. 16): “In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s kingdom, Basha, the king of Yisrael, advanced.” Is it possible to say so?
