Had not Basha already died in the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, as it is written (Melachim I 16:8): “In the twenty-sixth year of Asa, king of Yehudah, Elah the son of Basha reigned”? What then is the meaning of “In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s kingdom”? This corresponds to the thirty-six years from the time that Shlomo married Paroh’s daughter, for so it is written (Melachim I 2:39-46): “and two of Shimi’s slaves ran away... And the king commanded Bnayahu etc. and he smote (Sic) and fell upon him,” and immediately following this Scripture writes about Shlomo’s marriage to Paroh’s daughter, i.e., immediately after those three years, and in the fourth year he married her, and he reigned forty years. We find that she was with him thirty-six years, and corresponding to them were the thirty-six years that the decree was issued upon the kings of Aram to be adversaries to Yisrael and finally to fall into the hand[s] of David’s sons. Therefore, it is stated: “In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s kingdom.” In the sixteenth year of his reign, after Zerach the Kushi fell into his hand[s], that is the thirty-sixth year from Shlomo’s death, and in the sixteenth [year] of Asa, the king of Yisrael and the king of Aram made a treaty to advance and provoke Asa. Asa sinned, as it is stated (16:2f.): “And Asa brought out silver and gold... saying, ‘Make (sic) a treaty between me and you...’ And Ben Hadad heeded.” And the kings of Aram did not cease being adversaries to Yisrael until Achaz died, and in the third year of Achaz, the king of Yisrael and the king of Aram made a treaty to advance and provoke Achaz, and Achaz had no merit that they should fall into his hand[s]; so they both fell into the hand [s] of Tiglath-Pileser, the king of Ashur.

in Damesek And in Melachim I (15:18) it is written, “Damesek,” and in another verse (Melachim II 16: 10) it is written, “Dumesek.” It is all the same, an example being שׁוֹט, שֵׁבֶט, שַׁרְבִיט, whip, rod, scepter.

therefore...escaped You did not prevail against them. Why not? Because you did not trust in the Holy One, blessed be He. For had you trusted in the Holy One, blessed be He, when the king of Yisrael and the king of Aram made a treaty against you, as you trusted in Him when the Kushim attacked you, they would not have escaped from your hand, and you would have defeated them all, and you would not have lost your money, which you gave him in order that he abrogate his treaty with Basha. Now that you did not trust in the Holy One, blessed be He, you lost your money, and the king of Aram escaped from your hand.
into the prison house - Heb. בֵּית הַמַּהְפֶּכֶת. A prison made of vaultwork, gewelb(e)t in Middle High German, vaulted (prison).
until his ailment spread upward The swelling in his feet spread from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.
and divers kinds These are kinds of spices, and the spices were prepared with the perfumer’s art, a mixture. The meaning is: prepared with the perfumer’s art.

and they kindled an exceedingly great fire They burned good spices for him into ashes, and they scattered those ashes on him. Others explain this like (Abodah Zarah 11a): “We may burn for the kings.” Now what did they burn? Their biers and the utensils they used.

in the first ways of David, his father But not the last ways, when he sinned in the incident of Bat Sheva, and when the Adversary enticed him to count Yisrael. This is the most accurate interpretation, but others explain “first” as meaning superior to Shlomo and Rechavam. Regarding Shlomo, it is written (Melachim I 11:4): “his wives turned away his heart” at the end of his days, and he built a high place for Kmosh, the abomination of Moav, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Amon.” Regarding Rechavam, it is written (above 12:1): “And when he became strong, he abandoned the Law of Hashem.” [Yehoshafat was also not] like Aviyam, about whom it is written (Melachim I 15:2): “and his heart was not complete with Hashem, his Elokim,” or like Asa, who did not rely on Hashem; [Yehoshafat] resembled his father, David, who had only one heart for his Father in heaven.
and did not inquire of the baalim like the practice of Yisrael in his time, for Achav, who was in his time, worshipped the baalim, as did Yisrael in his time.

And his heart was uplifted in the ways of Hashem His heart was lifted up in this matter, that he went only in the ways of Hashem. An example of this is (Shemot 35:26): “whose hearts had uplifted them in wisdom.”

Ben Hail That was his name. Others explain: he sent to his officers, every officer a valiant man. But I have difficulty with this interpretation because, if so, it should have only said, “Ovadyah.” The fact that it says, “to Ovadyah” proves that Ben Hail was a person’s name.
to teach in the cities of Yehudah [i.e., to teach] the Torah and to instruct the Children of Yisrael.
And with them of the Leviyim were Shmayah, Netanyah, etc.

and with them were Elishama and Yehoram, the priests because it is incumbent upon the priests and the Leviyim to teach and to instruct, as it is written (Devarim 24:8): “in accordance with everything the priests, the Leviyim teach you.” The officers went with them because they [the people] would not disobey their orders, and [the officers went] to coerce them [the people] to heed them [the priests] and to observe [and] to do in accordance with the order of the judges. An example (ibid. 15:18): “Judges and law-enforcing officials shall you appoint for yourself”: Judges to judge the people, and law-enforcing officials to coerce them to comply with the orders of the judges.
And the fear of Hashem was upon all the kingdoms of the lands in the merit of having studied Torah.
and loads of silver - Heb. וְכֶסֶף מַשָּׂא, loads of silver. An example (Yeshayahu 46:1): “נְשֻׂאתֵיכֶם עֲמוּסוֹת מַשָּׂא: the things that you carried are made a load.”

was becoming greater - Heb. וְגָדֵל. Scripture uses] a similar expression in reference to three people: Yitzchak, Shmuel, and Yehoshafat, but concerning Moshe, David, and Mordechai, it says וְגָדוֹל. Concerning Yitzchak, Shmuel, and Yehoshafat, it says, וְגָדֵל because it is not proper to say וְגָדוֹל, great [in the context in which the word appears in the verse]. In regards to Shmuel, it says, (Shmuel I 2: 21): “And the lad Shmuel grew up with Hashem.” Hashem forbid that it should say, גָדוֹל עִם ה', he was great with Hashem. Here too, he [Yehoshafat] became great to an unusual degree, גָדֵל עַד לְמָעְלָה. It is therefore improper to say וְגָדוֹל, great. The same applies to Yitzchak.
towers בִּירָנִיוֹת, derived from בִּירָה, huge towers for strength.
and store cities storage cities, to put in them wheat, wine and grain.
And beside him Heb. וְעַל יָדוֹ beside him; an example is (Shmuel II 14:30): “Yoav’s field is adjoining mine (אֶל יָדִי).”
who gave generously to Hashem - Heb. הַמִּתְנַדֵּב. An example is (Jud. 5:2) “when the people offer themselves willingly (בְּהִתְנַדֵּב עַם), bless Hashem”

And he went down at the end of years And in Melachim I (22:2) it is written: “And it was in the third year, that Yehoshafat came down, etc.” This refers to the third year since he had released Ben Hadad (ibid. 20:34).

and he enticed him to go up to Ramot Gilad as is written in the Book of Melachim I (22: 3): “Do you know that Ramot Gilad is ours,” because when Yaakov built the mound [of stones] there and called it Galead, he took possession of it, and our forefathers took Gilad and the heights (רָמוֹת), which are a continuation and an attachment to the city. But when our forefathers in Moshe’s time seized Gilad, they were silent and refrained from taking it, because they did not care for it, or perhaps in Moshe’s time, they did take it, but later the nations took it from Yisrael’s hands, but it is [in fact] ours.
Please inquire today the word of Hashem and [do not inquire] of the prophets of the baalim in whom you trust.

And the king of Yisrael gathered the prophets, four hundred And they were all true prophets, for he gathered for Yehoshafat that which he had requested of him. And this is proven in the closely following text (verse 20f.): “And a spirit came forth, etc. and said: ‘I will entice him...and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets,’ for I will inspire them to say to Achav: Ascend, and Hashem will deliver it into the hands of the king.” From here we can deduce that they were prophets of Hashem, for they prophesied only the word of Hashem, for if they were false prophets, they would not entice, for they would prophesy only that which they were inventing from their minds. Moreover, Yehoshafat later said, “Is there no other prophet of Hashem?” I know that they are prophets of Hashem, but I have a tradition from my grandfather’s house that two prophets do not prophesy in the same style and with the same language, but all of these [prophets] are [unanimously] prophesying, “Ascend and prosper.”
but always bad For this is what it says (Melachim I 20:42): “Because you have released the man whom I designated for destruction, etc.”
Bring Michayhu at once [Michayhu] is written with the “yud” missing. He called him by a different name, Micahu, in order to degrade him.

dressed in [their] attire the royal raiment and seated in a threshing floor He is telling us that when the prophets prophesied before them, they were sitting outside the city, and spies of the king of Aram came there and heard that he [the prophet] informed the king of Yisrael that he alone would fall in battle. That is the reason that the king of Aram commanded his forces (v. 30): “Attack neither small nor great; only the king of Yisrael,” to fulfill the words of Michayhu. That is why it is written, “in a threshing floor,” for it was a place where spies could spy. If the meeting had been inside the city, the spies of the king of Aram would not have been able to infiltrate, for they would have detected that they were spies; but when they were outside the city, even if they [Bnei Yisrael] became aware of them, they could say, “We are going elsewhere, and the reason we drew near to the threshing floor is because of the great tumult and gathering of the armies here at the gate of the city; we were amazed, and turned off the road to see what was going on.” Consequently, the spies informed the king of Aram [what they had heard], who commanded to slay no one but the king of Yisrael. Otherwise, why did it enter his mind to command not to slay anyone of Yisrael, but the king? But he had spies who had heard Michayhu saying, (verses 16f.): “I saw all Bnei Yisrael scattered, etc. And the Lord said: These have no master.” This was a sign that the king would be slain, and that Bnei Yisrael would return each one to his house in peace. And they heard that he said, (v. 27): “If you return in peace...” The spies heard all and informed the king of Aram. The king of Aram then commanded to act in accordance with the word of Michayhu, and to slay only the king.
Go up and triumph, and may they be delivered into your hand i.e., May you only prosper, and may they be delivered into your hands.

scattered over the mountains For when they flee from battle, they flee on the mountains to a refuge, like (Bereshit 14:10): “and those who remained fled to the mountains.” In addition, the battle was on the heights of Gilad, a mountainous and hilly terrain.
And Hashem said: These have no master They are scattered like sheep on the mountains, because they have no shepherd, for their king will be slain.
Let them return each one to his house in peace Achav alone will be killed, but the rest of Bnei Yisrael will return each one to his house in peace, as the king of Aram commanded his people.
and all the host of heaven were standing on His right and His left These are the angels of destruction who stand before Him.

And a certain spirit came forth The meaning is: And an angel came forth, for he says above, “and all the host of heaven, etc.” One of the angels came forth and said, “I will entice him,” as it is stated (Tehillim 104:4): “He makes His angels spirits.” [Cf. Comm. Dig. ad loc.] He preceded this account by stating, “and all the host of heaven were standing,” so that you should not wonder when you read, “And a certain spirit came forth,” who he was and where he came from. When he says, “and all the host of heaven were standing,” it is to inform you where he came from: from among the rest of the spirits standing beside Him. Our Rabbis (Sanh. 89a, Targum) however, explained that this was the spirit of Navot.

in the mouth of all his prophets He should place the words “Go up and triumph,” in their mouths and he [Achav] will go up and fall. This proves that they were true prophets who would prophesy only that which Hashem put into their mouths.

You will entice and you will prevail When an enticer comes to entice his fellow, the one being enticed sometimes understands that this one wishes to entice him, and he takes heed and does not allow himself to be enticed, but with Achav, you will entice and you will prevail.
Behold you will see that Achav will be killed.

Place this person in prison We did not see that he incarcerated him in prison previously, but since he says, “and return him,” you may say that he had placed him in prison beforehand. If, however, you wish to say that they had never placed him in prison prior to this, “and return him” should not cause you any difficulty, because this is the style of the Scriptures, like (Tehillim 9:18): “May the wicked return to the grave,” and many similar other cases.
a scant amount of bread, etc. An example of this is (Yeshayahu 30: 20): “scant bread and water of oppression.”

disguise myself and go The meaning is: “I must make myself like a stranger and disguise myself in other clothes, so that they do not recognize that I am the king of Yisrael,” for he was wary of Michayhu’s words, saying, “If you return in peace, etc.” And he said to Yehoshafat, “I wish to disguise myself and go to war, for I fear that the Aram heard that Michayhu said, ‘If you return in peace,’ and they will attack only me.”

but you may wear your garb The royal costume and the coat of mail and the royal weapons, for there is no need for anyone to be wary of the prophet’s words except the king of Yisrael, for his [the king of Aram’s] spies told [him] the words of Michayhu.

and Yehoshafat cried out He called to his troop and his armies to come to his aid, [using] the sign of the lion on his banner or the banner of the sons of Yehudah. And so is the custom when two troops engage in battle: each troop gives a name to the insignia of its division for the troop that is with it, so that if they separate from each other or if the troops mingle with one another, each troop shouts the name of its insignia, and they recognize the insignia and all gather together and become one group as originally. He did not, however, cry out to his Elokim, as is proven from Melachim I (22:32), for there it does not say, “and Hashem helped him, and Elokim enticed them away from him,” but it is written, And it was when the officers of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Yisrael for they immediately recognized and understood when he cried out the insignia of his division, as was explained. As soon as they recognized him, they turned away from him in accordance with the order of the king of Aram, and it was from Hashem that they recognized him.
And a man drew his bow A Yisraeli man intended to shoot at the camp of Aram, and inadvertently
and it hit The arrow [hit] the king of Yisrael.

between the scales and the coat of mail between the thong with which they attach the helmet on his head to the coat of mail. We cannot say that he was a heathen, because whom was he aiming at? Did not the king of Aram command, “Attack neither small nor great, except the king of Yisrael”? And he did not even aim at him, for it is written, “innocently.” Perforce, you must say that the archer was a Yisraeli who intended to shoot at the camp of Aram, and inadvertently hit the king of Yisrael.
and he said to the charioteer to the one who drives the chariot.
and carry me out of the camp i.e., away from these front lines, and take me to the rear lines.

And the battle withdrew It withdrew, and not one of Yisrael was hurt except the king of Isra el, in accordance with the word of the prophet, (above verse 16): “These have no master. Let them return each one to his house in peace.” It does not say לְשָלוֹם, because Achav was slain.
was standing in the chariot He exerted himself and stood up so that Bnei Yisrael should not realize that he was wounded and flee, for the beginning of defeat is fleeing.
for you have abolished the asheroth as above (17:6), “and he removed the high places [and the asherim], etc.”
to seek Elokim as above (17:4): “but he inquired of the Elokim of his father, etc.”

And he appointed judges When the seer told him, “good things were found in you, for you abolished the asheroth,” he approached the Sepher Torah [to see] whether he had abolished them properly. He first saw that it was written (Devarim 12:2f.): “You shall utterly destroy...and you shall burn their asherim with fire and cut down the images of their gods,” and he remembered that it is written in כִּי תִשָׂא (Shemot 34:13): “And you shall break down their monuments, etc.” He wondered why he had pleased Hashem by abolishing the asherim, the Jewish asherim, for [the Torah] only warned about their asherim. He went back to [the Torah portion] (Devarim 16:18): “Judges and law enforcing agents,” and found written (verse 21): “You shall not plant an asherah.” Then he rejoiced that he had abolished them. He also saw written there: “Judges and law enforcing agents you shall appoint for yourself,” and immediately “he appointed judges,” strong ones.

in all the fortified cities of Yehudah, for every city He first appointed strong [judges] in all the fortified cities of Yehudah to coerce them [the people] and compel them to [accept] judgment. He later appointed judges who were not as strong for the cities that were not fortified, for they [the inhabitants] were more afraid to rebel than those who dwelt in the fortified cities, for they felt secure in their fortified cities.

for you do not judge for man The meaning is: Do not think in your heart: What difference does it make if we pervert the law to declare our friends innocent and pervert the rights of the poor and favor the rich? Is it not so that the judgment is not for Hashem? Therefore, it says, “for Hashem.” It is for Him. If you convict the innocent, it is as though you take from your Creator’s property and pervert the law of Heaven, by bestowing a distorted verdict. Therefore, “see what you are doing,” and may your heart be in every judgment, as if the Holy One, blessed be He, is standing before you in judgment, and this is the meaning of: “and [He] is with you in the matter of the judgment.” In Sanhedrin (6b) it is stated “What are you doing, for you do not judge for man but for Hashem.” This is explained [as follows]: Perhaps the judge will say, “How does this problem concern me?” Therefore, Scripture states: “and it is with you concerning the matter of the judgment,” i.e., it is incumbent upon you to rule justly. And the judge must deal only with that which he sees with his own eyes.
for with Hashem your Elokim there is neither injustice, favoritism, nor bribe-taking and He is with you in judgment; therefore, He does not wish you to commit injustice in judgment.
And also in Yerushalayim...set up judges even though he himself was in Yerushalayim.

for the judgment of Hashem and for quarrels It is appropriate to use the term “judgment” (לְמִשְׁפַּט) concerning money matters, an example being (Bamidbar 27:11) “and it shall be for the Children of Yisrael as a legal norm (לְחֻקַּת מִשְׁפָּט).” “And for quarrels” (וְלָרִיב) refers to capital cases and bodily injuries, an example being (Shemot 21:18) “And if men quarrel, etc.” (יְרִיבוּן).

So shall you do Because of alacrity, caution, and encouragement, he added a “nun,” like (Bereshit 32: 5): “So shall you say (תאמְרוּן),” and like (Rut 2:8f.): “and here you shall stay (תִדְבָּקִין) with my maidens. Your eyes shall be on the field that they reap (יִִִקְצרוּן),” and like (ibid. 3:18): “until you know (תֵּדְעִין) how the matter will be resolved, for the man will not rest, etc.”
between blood[shed] and blood[shed] between the bloodshed of an unintentional murder and an intentional one.
you shall admonish them your brethren.
and there be wrath upon you and upon your brethren Therefore so shall you do You shall admonish your brethren.

and you will not be guilty In any case, you [will not be guilty], for if you accept the admonition, there will be no wrath upon you, and there will also be no guilt upon you in anything since you performed the duty which was incumbent upon you to perform.
and may Hashem be with the good with the one who performs that which is good and upright.

and with them, some of Bnei Amon This is Amalek. Why were they called Bnei Amon? Because they changed their dress and their language to resemble that of Bnei Amon and mingled with them, and came to wage war against Yisrael. This can be proven below in the chapter (verse 22): “And at the time they commenced, etc. Hashem placed liers-in-wait against the children of Amon, Moav, and Mount Seir.” We find that Bnei Amon mentioned here are Amaleki who changed their tongue and their dress. This is what the Kallir set down in the section of Zachor: Remember the tyrant who hid among Bnei Amon; he breached the vineyards of Ein-Gedi when he was brought, i.e., remember what Amaleki the tyrant did - he hid among Bnei Amon and came to breach the vineyards of Yisrael at that time, as it is written: “and behold they are in Hazazon-Tamar which is Ein-Gedi,” and Ein-Gedi is close to the territory of Amalek, as is stated in (Bereshit 14:7): “and they struck down the whole field of the Amaleki, and also the Emori who dwell in Hazazon- Tamar.”
the same is Ein-Gedi i.e., They said to him, “They have already come so close to us.”

also from all the cities of Yehudah That you should not say, when it is stated initially, “And the Yehudim gathered to seek,” that these were the inhabitants of Yerushalayim only, but they came from all the cities of Yehudah.
and that You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations and in Your hand is strength and might to conduct Your rule over them; therefore, we beseech You to save us from them.
and in Your hand is strength and might in wars and might, hardiess in French, boldness.

and no one can stand with You No creature can stand against You of all the kingdoms of the nations, and an example of this is (Yehoshua 1:5): “No man shall stand before You.” (Rabbi Menachem the son of Helbo explained it in this manner.)

and given it to the seed of Avraham Therefore, it is incumbent upon You to preserve it in their hands and to drive these peoples out. Even a flesh and blood king, and even an ordinary man, when he gives a present to his friend and someone comes to rob him of it, he exerts himself to preserve it in his hand. How much more so [should] You [do so]! Perhaps You will say, “I gave it to them only temporarily.” Therefore, it says, “forever.” You gave it to us for an eternal inheritance.
and therein they built You a Sanctuary for Your name, saying that “should evil come upon us, etc.” judgment or any judgment, whether sword, pestilence, or famine.
and we shall cry out to You from our distress in the Temple.

and You will hear and save as Shlomo prayed before You, and You promised him to do so, as is written (above 6:24): “And if Your people is struck down,” continuing with the entire chapter until (verse 30): “and forgive and give to each man according to his ways.” And Hashem accepted his prayer, as it is written (ibid. 7:12): “And Hashem appeared to Shlomo, and said to him: I have heard your prayer,” continuing with the entire chapter until (ibid. verse 14) “and forgive their sin and heal their land.” Now I pray that You remember the promise which You promised him, and hear and save us from our enemies who are coming upon us.
And now about all that You promised us to save us from our enemies who are coming upon us.
behold the children of Amon and Moav and Mount Seir, against whom You did not permit Yisrael to come to wage war.

when they came out of the land of Mitzrayim and they should have remembered the kindness [we performed] and come to our aid, but they - not only did they not remember our kindness, to be with us in all our troubles, but they repayed us with evil and attacked us.
to drive us out of Your inheritance, which You caused us to inherit You Yourself. Therefore, on what basis can they contest our inheritance?
but our eyes are upon You to save us.
also their infants It is customary that when troops attack a country, the infants, wives, and children flee the villages to the fortified cities.

You shall not fear, neither shall you be dismayed This refers back to what they said, (verse 12) “we have no strength before this multitude.” The prophet said to them, “Although they outnumber you, do not fear them.”

for the war is not yours but Elokim’s This refers back to (verse 12) “and we do not know,” and the prophet replied, “It is surely as you have said, that your eyes and your trust are upon the Holy One, blessed be He, to save you.” So will He do, for the war is not yours but Elokim’s.
on the ascent to Haziz the name of a place.
set yourself This refers back to (verse 15) “for the war is not yours.”

and see the salvation of Hashem This refers back to the above: “Have You, our Elokim, not caused us to inherit (sic)?” And the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, “You are right. It is up to Me to preserve it in your hands.”
Tomorrow go forth before them and I shall wage war on your behalf. And they believed, and hurried, and arose early in the morning.
and you will be believed Heb. וְתֵאָמֵנוּ. You will be trustworthy and prosper. An example is (Yeshayahu 7: 9) “for you cannot be believed (לֹא תֵאָמֵנוּ).”

Hashem placed liers-in-wait He placed liers-in-wait to annihilate them and destroy them. An example is found in the case of Aviyah the son of Rechavam (13:13): “And Yerovam turned the ambush.” Similarly, the Holy One, blessed be He, turned them one against another, and later, Moav returned and aided the children of Amon, and they both rose up against the children of Seir.

when they finished with the inhabitants of Seir, each one helped his friend to destroy The Holy One, blessed be He, turned one against the other until they were completely destroyed; until the corpses fell to the ground with no survivors.
to the extent that they could not carry them away because of the quantity.

they congregated to the valley of Berachah To the valley which was later called the valley of Berachah, because of the incident [that took place there], as is explained immediately following, as Scripture states for there they blessed Hashem and gave thanks for all the good that He had done for them, that He saved them from their enemies.
And they came to Yerushalayim with psalteries, with harps, and with trumpets These three musical instruments correspond to “all the men of Yehudah and Yerushalayim and Yehoshafat.”

And he went in the way of his father Asa and did not turn away From what did he not turn away? to do what was right From the good and upright way of his father he did not turn away, but from the bad ways of Asa he did turn away, as is written (above 16:2): “And Asa brought forth silver and gold,” and the entire incident, but Yehoshafat did not do so, but trusted in the Holy One, blessed be He, all his life.
in the words of Yehu the son of Chanani who said to King Yehoshafat, (19:2) “[Did you go] to aid the wicked?”
and could not go - Heb. וְלֹא עָצְרוּ, lit., they did not hold in. The meaning is: The ships could not muster the strength to go, and they were broken.
a kingdom - Heb. נִיר. Its meaning is a yoke over Yisrael.

In his days, Edom rebelled, etc. For David had destroyed all the males in Edom, and he appointed governors over them instead of a king, and they paid him tribute, and all the kings of Yehudah did similarly: they appointed governors who pleased them. And from the days of Yoram and thereafter, they [the Edomim] rebelled against the authority of Yehudah.

who surrounded him He smote those Edomim who surrounded him and supported him to aid him, for it was their custom that when they were victorious in war, they would seize the mighty men and bring them with them lest they join their enemies to aid the Edomim, their countrymen. In this case, he got up at night suddenly and slew them. Our Sages, however, explained “those who surrounded him” as “those near him.”

And Edom rebelled Was it not already stated above (verse 8): “In his days, Edom rebelled?” But this is the manner of Scripture: because a verse is interposed, and it now wishes to continue with “then Livnah rebelled,” it repeats the [original words] stating, “And Edom rebelled.” then Livnah rebelled It belonged to Yehudah, and it was situated on the border of Edom, as is written in the Book of Yehoshua (15:21, 42): “And the outermost cities of the tribe of the children of Yehudah toward the border of Edom.” When they saw that the Edomim rebelled, they too rebelled, for they lived on the border of Edom, and they aided Edom. This is [the meaning of] “then Livnah rebelled.”

because he had forsaken Hashem, the Elokim of his forefathers [Scripture] explains what it was that caused them to rebel in his time more than during [the time of] the rest of the kings of Yehudah who preceded him.

and led the inhabitants of Yerushalayim astray - Heb. זְנוּת. It is appropriate to use the term harlotry in connection with anyone who forsakes and exchanges the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, for the idolatry of star and planet worship - for such a person behaves in the manner of a promiscuous woman who commits adultery with others, and similar to this are (Devarim 31:16): “and this people will rise and go astray (וְזָנָה) after the foreign gods of the land”; (Hoshea 1:2): “for the land will go astray (זָנה תִזְנֶה), etc.”
And a letter came to him from Eliyahu After he had ascended to heaven, this prophetic letter came to him [i.e., to Yoram].

and split it - Heb. וַיִִּבְקָעוּהָ, like (Yeshayahu 7:6): “Let us go up to Yehudah and provoke it and breach its walls וְנַבְקִעֶנָה and so, (Melachim II 3:26): “to break a way (לְהַבְקִיעַ)o the king of Edom.”
and at the end the end that the prophet had foretold him of.

and his people did not make him a burning even though he required that burning because he had been ailing with malignant illnesses, and his flesh reeked. The Holy One, blessed be He, did not wish to honor him by making a burning for him, and he was also not buried in the graves of the kings.

and he departed joyless The meaning is: all his life he was in distress and in illnesses, and with him was fulfilled (Devarim 30:15): “See, I have set before you today life, etc.” and (Iyov 14:1) “short of days and full of fear.”

forty two years old But in Melachim II (8:26), Scripture says: “twenty-two years old.” How is this possible? Moreover, according to this, the son was two years his father’s senior, [because Yoram ascended the throne at thirty-two and died eight years later, making him forty years old upon his death,] but two years before Yoram his father was born, this decree was issued upon the house of David that it would end with the house of Achav, and so Scripture states (below verse 7): “And from Elokim was Achazyahu’s downfall, etc.” and on the day that Asa took Omri’s daughter for Yehoshafat his son, this decree was issued. So it was taught in Seder Olam (ch. 17) and in the Tosefta of Sotah (12:3). But throughout Scripture we do not find that Yehoshafat married Omri’s daughter, but I did find (above 18:1): “and he allied himself in marriage with Achav,” and perhaps that was his sister that he married, and in the thirty first year of Asa he married her, as it is said in (Melachim I 16:23): “And (sic) in the thirty-first year of Asa, etc. Omri reigned.” And when Asa married his daughter to Yehoshafat his son, Omri gained importance, and they slew Tivni. Figure from the thirty-first year of Asa until Achazyahu reigned, and you will find forty two years. Further, one verse states (Melachim II 8:25): “In the twelfth year of Yoram the son of Achav, etc., Achazyahu the son of Yoram reigned,” and another verse states (ibid. 9:29): “And in the eleventh year of Yoram son of Achav, Achazyahu became king.” Perforce, his father did not die until the twelfth year of Yoram son of Achav, because it is written (ibid. 8: 16f.): “In the fifth year of Yoram the son of Achav, etc., Yoram the son of Yehoshafat became king, etc., and he reigned eight years.” And that which Scripture states further, “In the eleventh year of Yoram,” is because he reigned one year during his father’s lifetime since his father was smitten with severe illnesses, as it is written (above 21:18.): “And after all this, Hashem plagued him, etc.” (22: 1) “And the inhabitants of Yerushalayim made Achazyahu, his youngest son, king,” for one year during his father’s lifetime, and that is what is written: “In the eleventh year of Yoram.” And where Scripture says: “In the twelfth year of Yoram,” it means that after his father died, it was the twelfth year of Yoram.

and the Aram smote Yoram - Heb. הָרַמִּים, like הָאֲרַמִּים. In many places the “aleph” is missing, as for instance (Shmuel II 19:14): “And to Amasa you shall say (תֹמְרוּ).” And sometimes the “aleph” is added to a word, for instance (Tehillim 89:1): “Eitan the Ezrachi (הָאֶזְרָחִי),” like הַזַּרְחִי, [descendant of Zerach], and the “aleph” of (Iyov 13:17): “and to my speech (וְאַחְוָתִי) in your ears.”
because of the smiters who smote him כִּי הַמַּכִּים. The meaning is: מִן הַמַּכִּים, because of the smiters, and so it is in Melachim II (8:29).
and Azaryah the son of Yehoram This is Achazyahu, and so Scripture states (ad loc.): “and Achazyahu the son of Yoram went down to see Yoram.”
downfall Heb. תְּבוּסַת. The meaning is confusion, like (Yechezkel 16:6): “wallowing (מִתְבּוֹסֶסֶת) in your blood.”

and the sons of Achazyahu’s brothers He does not mention Achazyahu’s brothers because they were slain in the days of Yoram their father, as it is written (above 21:17): “And they marched upon Yehudah and split it, etc., and no son was left to him except Yehoachaz, the youngest of his sons.”

she arose and destroyed - Heb. וַתְּדַבֵּר, an expression of דֶּבֶר, pestilence. In Melachim II (11:1), it is written: וַתְּאַבֵּד. Concerning this generation, David recited: (Tehillim 12:1): “For the conductor on the sheminith,” for David foresaw with the holy spirit that in the eighth generation [of his dynasty] all his descendants would be slain by Atalyahu, for there are eight generations from Shlomo till here. And he prayed that his seed would survive for a remembrance, and said, (ibid. verse 2): “Save, O Hashem, for the pious are gone, etc.” In Melachim II (11:2), Scripture states that she killed them by poisoning them, for it is written: “and she stole him away from the dying (הַמְמוֹתִים) children of the king”; we read: הַמּוּמָתִים the slain. Both the traditional reading and the masoretic text have authority. הַמּוּמָתִים means that they already died, and the masoretic text in which the word used is הַמְמוֹתִים means that they were dying in agony. This is written in the continuous present tense, i.e., not all at once but continuously being crushed by illnesses, and then dying. An example is (Yirmiyahu 16:4): “Dying of (מְמוֹתֵי) sicknesses they shall die, etc. and with famine,” because they too will not die immediately.

in the bed chamber The Targum [Yonatan to Melachim II 11:2] renders: in the chamber of the beds, i.e., in the forecourt, in the room where the priests sleep, but Rabbi Shlomo of blessed memory (Rashi ad loc) explained it as the attic of the Holy of Holies, as it is written in Kings (verse 3): “And he hid with her in the House of Hashem, etc.,” and concerning him, David said, (Tehillim 27:5): “For He will hide me in His Tabernacle, etc.” He calls it the bed chamber based on (Shir Hashirim 1:13): “between my breasts he will lie,” and that is what the Kallir, Rabbi Eliezer Kara composed (in Zichronoth for the first day of Rosh Hashanah in the section devoted to the letter “nun”): If He said to cause them to totter, the smashing of the bed-chamber He will remember for an atonement. The destruction of the Temple will atone for them.
And the entire congregation enacted a covenant in the House of Elokim with the king that they would support him.

of those coming in on the Sabbath And also those leaving on the Sabbath, as is written below (verse 8): “and each one took his men, those coming in on the Sabbath with those leaving on the Sabbath.” The watches were renewed on the Sabbath (See Taanith 2:6,7), viz. the priests and the Leviyim; one [watch] would leave and one would come in. Yehoyada detained the watch that was leaving with the watch that was coming in, and divided them into three divisions.
And a third shall be in the king’s palace to guard that they would not gather about him to assassinate him.
and a third This is the second one.

in the Yesod Gate But in II Kings (ad loc.) it is written “the Sur Gate.” In Yoma Yerushalmi (in extant editions it is found in Erubin Yerushalmi 5:1) it is explained that the Yesod Gate had seven names: 1) the Sur Gate, because they would purify those smitten with zaraath there [by placing the blood of the guilt offering and the oil] on their thumbs, reminiscent of [the verse] (Eichah 4:15): “They called out to them: ‘Depart (סוּרוּ), unclean [ones]!’”
and all the people shall keep lest they enter the House of Hashem.
with his weapons in his hand His weapons in his hand.

of those coming in on the Sabbath with those leaving on the Sabbath, for he did not dismiss those divisions who were leaving to go home, but he detained them with those who were arriving. A similarity to [the word פָּטַר] is found in (Divrei Hayamim I 9:33): “in the chambers, who are exempt (פְּטוּרִים)”; i.e., they were exempt from all work in the forecourt, for day and night it was incumbent upon them to perform the work to guard the forecourts and the chambers; they were therefore exempt from all other work in the forecourt.
and each one with his sword in his hand - Heb. שִׁלְחוֹ his weapon, like (Yoel 2:8): “and upon the sword (הַשֶּׁלַח).”

the crown This is the crown that David took from Rabbah of the children of Amon, as it is written (Divrei Hayamim I 20:2): “And David took the crown of Malkam off his head, etc., and it was on David’s head.” From then on, the kings of Yehudah would wear that crown on their heads.

and the testimony This is a Sepher Torah, and so Scripture states (Devarim 17:19): “and he shall read from it as long as he lives.” Our Sages stated (Abodah Zarah 4a), however, that the crown itself was the testimony, for it would not fit anyone unfit for the throne.

standing on his stand as it says (above 6:12f.): “And he stood before the altar of the Lord, etc. for Shlomo had made a copper laver, etc., and he stood on it and kneeled on his knees.” It is still customary today that when they assemble together, the king or the duke stands on a high place, so that they should be able to see him and hear his words.
“Treason! Treason!” Rebellion! Rebellion!

the ranks - Heb. הַשְּׂדֵרוֹת. Rashi (Melachim II 11:8) explains: the place of the king’s entry from his palace to the House of Hashem. I do not know the origin of the word, and Yonatan rendered it as “rows” [like סְדָרִים].
and whoever follows her is to be put to death Do not allow her to go out by way of the exit of the forecourt to the city, lest she find helpers who will join her.
and whoever follows her to her aid.
is to be put to death Put him to death.
And they made a place for her a place to escape.
between himself and all the people and the king that all of them, the king and the people, should follow Hashem.

appointees - Heb. פְּקֻדּוֹת, people appointed to offer burnt offerings and all that is mentioned in this chapter. An example is (Yirmiyahu 20:1): “And Pashchur heard, etc. and he was the chief officer (פָּקִיד) in the House of Hashem.”
so that no one who was unclean should enter for any matter There were also appointees [whose job it was] not to allow any unclean person to enter the forecourt for any reason.

all the days of Yehoyada And in Melachim II (12:3) it is written: “all his days, [he did] that which Yehoyada the priest instructed him,” but after he died, the officers of the king came to prostrate themselves to him and to deify him (below verse 17). In the midrash (Exod. Rabbah 8:2, Tan. Buber, Va’era) it is explained that, because he hid in the Holy of Holies and was not harmed, they said, “You are fit to be a god.”
and he begot sons and daughters Because it says below (verse 25) that Yoash slew the sons of Yehoyada, it was necessary to note that he had sons.

and gather money from all Yisrael i.e., Gather the money that Bnei Yisrael were accustomed to giving yearly, as it is written (Shemot 30:14): “Each one included in the census,” and in Melachim II (12: 5): “All money of the hallowed things that is brought to the House of Hashem, in current money, etc.” There were three types of money: (1) the money of all those counted in the census, viz. the shekels for every year, as it is said (Shemot 30:14): “Each one included in the census,” lit., “[the money of anyone] who passes,” reminiscent of “each one who passes.” (2) Personal donations - money donated by individuals to reflect the value of their souls, like one who says, “My value shall be incumbent upon me to donate.” (3) All donations inspired by a person’s heart for the repairs of the Temple.

and hasten to the matter,” but the Leviyim did not hasten It is explained in Melachim II (12:6f.) that the king said, “Let the priests take [the money] for themselves, each one from his acquaintance,” but they neglected to impose upon their acquaintances, and when the king saw this, he said to them, (ibid. verse 8): “Do not take money from your acquaintances [any longer], but deliver it for the repairs of the House.” This is what is written here: “’and hasten to the matter,’ but the Leviyim did not hasten.”
the tax of Moshe the servant of Hashem i.e., the shekels which he mandated upon them in the desert.
the tax of - Heb. מַשְׂאַת, reminiscent of (Shemot 30:12): “When you take (כִּי תִשָּׂא) [the sum].”

For the wicked Atalyahu—her sons had breached He had to say this because Shlomo had built it as a new sturdy edifice. Only 125 years elapsed from the time that Shlomo built it until the days of Yoash and it was already breached. Had Atalyahu and her sons not breached it, it would have continued to endure, for more than 200 years elapsed from Yoash to Yoshiyahu and they did not have to repair it until Yoshiyahu, although Yoash did not make it new as it was originally. One hundred and twenty-five years elapsed from the completion of the Temple until Yoash. How so? Shlomo reigned 40 years, and in the fourth year of his reign he commenced to build it. It took 7 years to build, totaling 10 years, leaving him 30. Rechavam reigned 17, totaling 47; Aviyah 3, totaling 50; Asa 41, totaling 91; Yehoshafat 25, totaling 116; Yehoram 8, totaling 124, and Achazyahu one, totaling 125. And from Yoash until Yoshiyahu were 200 years. How so? Amatzyahu reigned 29 years, Uziyahu 52, Yotam 16, Achaz 16, Chizkiyahu 29, Menashe 55, Amon 2, totaling 200 less 1, in addition to those years that Yoash lived after he had repaired the Temple. We find that they would not have had to repair the damage of the Temple had not the wicked Atalyahu and her sons breached it.

For Atalyahu, etc. It is therefore no wonder that it needed repairs so soon, and also no wonder that there was no hallowed silver and gold in the treasuries of the House of Hashem, so that they had to make an announcement in Yehudah and Yerushalayim to bring the tax, for they had also used all the hallowed things of the House of Hashem for the baalim.

and they made one chest and in Melachim II (12:10), it is written: “and he bored a hole in its door,” and through that hole they would cast the hallowed things, but they did not open the door lest a thief come and steal from it.
and they placed it in the gate of the House of Hashem, to the outside so that all the generous people would be able to come and deposit the donation to Hashem therein.
and when they saw that there was much money then the king’s scribe came.

and the appointee of the head priest The servant appointed under the head priest, who was the assistant to the high priest, together with the king’s scribe. In Melachim II (12:11), it is written: “the king’s scribe and the high priest went up.” The meaning is that the king’s scribe went up, and the high priest also sent his appointee, who was the scribe who wrote what the high priest commanded him, because it was unfitting and degrading for the high priest to go with the king’s servants.
empty the chest - Heb. וִיעָרוּ. A similar instance is (Bereshit 24:20): “and emptied (וַתְּעַר) her pitcher.”

carry it Every day, when they saw that there was much money in it, they would bring it to the king’s appointee within the forecourt, empty it, carry it, and return it to its place outside the gate of Hashem.
and the work was improved A similar instance is (Nechemyah 3:34): “Will they revive the stones” of Ezra. Also, above (Divrei Hayamim I 11:8): “and Yoav sustained.’
on its base - Heb. עַל מַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ, on its base.

service vessels and pestles (Stessel in German.) This is [the implement] with which they crush spices in the mortar. A similar instance is (Mishlei 27:22): “If you crush a fool in a mortar [among grain with a pestle (בַּעֱלִי)”]. Rabbi Yitzchak the son of Shmuel of Narbonne told me this. Others say that וְהַעֲלוֹת refers to boards upon which meat is cut, and an example of this appears in Bezah (1:5): We may not move a board (עלי) to cut meat upon it.

and spoons and gold and silver vessels But in Melachim II (12:14) it is written: “But there would not be made for the House of Hashem silver pitchers.” How is this possible? It is explained in Kethuboth, chapter 13 (106): Rav Huna inquired of Rav: May vessels of ministry be made of material hallowed for the repair of the Temple, etc.

above the people Higher than the people, in order to make his voice heard. In Lamentations Rabbah (Proem 23), it is interpreted as meaning that he relied on himself; he was a prince higher than all the people, a prophet and a priest, and it was Yom Kippur, and he was the king’s son-in-law, and he was not afraid to say the prophecy. Concerning this incident, it was stated (Eichah 2:20): “shall priest and prophet be slain in the Sanctuary of Hashem?”

and upon his death, he said, “May Hashem see and requite.” For they have slain me only because I spoke as the Omnipresent’s medium, and since I have been slain for His sake, it is proper and fitting that He requite my blood. And so it was: his blood was immediately requited, for “it came to pass at the turn of the year, etc.”

And it came to pass at the turn of the year Because the sons of Yehudah sinned more than the other tribes, as it is written above (verse 18): “And they forsook the House of Hashem, the Elokim of their fathers.”

and they destroyed all the princes of the people This refers back to the above (verse 17): “And after the death of Yehoyada, the princes of Yehudah came and prostrated themselves to the king,” and caused Yoash to sin after them. Because of that, they were paid in kind: the army of Aram came and destroyed all the princes of the people.
from among the people from being a people.

for the blood of the sons of Yehoyada the priest Because of the blood of Zecharyah, who was the son of Yehoyada, for he should have remembered the favors and the loving-kindness that Yehoyada had bestowed upon him, and because of that iniquity, his servants conspired against him and slew him in his bed. They meted out to him a measure corresponding to a measure. Because Zecharyah was slain, tranquil and secure, with nothing to worry about, for he was the son of Yehoyada, and out of respect for him [Yehoyada], they respected him [Zecharyah], and spilled his blood onto the ground, therefore, he [Yehoash] too was slain in tranquility and security in his bed.

the Moabitess What difference does it make who they were and from whom they were descended? However, [Scripture means that] those ingrates who did not show their gratitude for the favor of Avraham our father to Lot their father, who fought with the kings when he heard that Lot was captured, and they hired Bilam to curse his sons; [they were chosen] to punish Yoash, who [similarly] did not show gratitude to Yehoyada and slew his son Zecharyah. It is explained this way in Mechilta (Shemot 17:8).

for Hashem is not with Yisrael, all the sons of Efraim because Yerovam was of the tribe of Efraim, and he was the first to cause Yisrael to sin. And in every generation thereafter he remained a stumbling block for them, for they worshipped the golden calves of Yerovam.
But if you come The meaning is: If you do not believe my words, will you not try [to put effort into your military campaign?] Come, do, and strengthen yourself for war.
to help or to cause to stumble The meaning is: He has the strength to help you without the army of Efraim and to cause you to stumble if you take them with you.
and they were all split open, etc...after [Amatzyahu] had come, etc. In Eichah Rabbah it says about him, “whether he is angry or he laughs” (Mishlei 29:9).

raided the cities of Yehudah from Shomron to Beth-Horon after they returned to their place, as above, “they were very angry with Yehudah and returned to their place.” For if it were not so, i.e., if they had raided the cities of Yehudah as soon as they left Amatzyahu, Scripture would have said, “and they raided the cities of Yehudah from Beth-Horon to Shomron,” [i.e., going from Yehudah to Shomron].

that Elokim has given counsel to destroy you i.e., If you do not hearken to My advice to follow the straight path, you should know, O king, that Hashem has given counsel to destroy you because you have done this, and have not hearkened to the counsel. Now what is the counsel? That he enticed you to provoke the king of Yisrael and to fall before him, as it is written: “And Amatzyahu the king of Yehudah took counsel, and he sent to Yoash, etc.”
Come, let us confront each other to show our might on horses with spears.
The thistle that was in Levanon which is of short stature.
sent to the cedar which is the greatest prince of all the trees.

passed by and trampled the thistle The cedar did not wish to kill it because it was degrading in his eyes to cut down the thistle, but a beast of the field passed by and trampled it in contempt, for how did he dare to send such a great insult to the lofty cedar? You too are like the thistle, for you have only two tribes, and now my servants will rise up against you and trample you when they hear of this disgrace.
and your heart has made you haughty to pursue glory, and you wish to be glorified also on my account. In Melachim II (14:10), the reading is: “Retain your honor by staying home.”
because this was from Elokim in order to deliver them into their hands i.e., into their hands, as above (verse 16): “I know that Elokim has given counsel to destroy you.”

in Beth-Shemesh the war took place. It was necessary to say this lest you ask why they brought Amatzyahu to Yerushalayim and not to Shomron when they seized him. [The answer is] that Beth-Shemesh was near Yerushalayim.
and breached the wall of... He said, “From now on, he will not rebel against me, because his heart will not be so haughty since the wall has been breached”
that were found in the House of Elokim with Obed-Edom for he and his sons were keepers of the treasures all their lives.

and the hostage children For the Yehudim did not permit Amatzyahu to be king any longer in Yerushalayim until he made the children of the officers hostages so that they would no longer rebel against him, and so did Jonathan translate it in Melachim II (14:14): “the children of the officers.” Rabbi Yosef (Kara) explained “the hostage children” to mean those hostages that the king had taken as security so that their fathers would not rebel against him. This, however, does not appear correct to me because we do not find that Yehudah had such power over others that they could have [forced them] to give Yehudah their children as hostages.

And from the time that Amatzyahu turned away from following Hashem and was defeated by the king of Yisrael, immediately they conspired against him in Yerushalayim to kill him, because each one was grieved over his son, his brother, and his kinsman who were slain because of him, because he provoked the king of Yisrael.

and he fled to Lachish a fortified city against which Sancheriv waged war. He fled to Lachish, where he remained fifteen years until they followed him to Lachish and assassinated him there. And during those fifteen years that he was in Lachish, Yecholyah, Uziyahu’s mother, reigned in his stead. This is how it appears to me. In the commentary of Rabbi Yosef (Kara), I saw that during those fifteen years that he was in Lachish, Uziyahu his son reigned in his stead, but it is incorrect to interpret it in this manner, for it is written immediately following (26:1): “who was sixteen years old.” We find that when his father fled, he was only one year old. Moreover, if this is the case, it should say, “took Uziyahu and made him king instead of his father during his lifetime.” Rather, Scripture intimated that he did not reign during his father’s lifetime.
And he did what was right in the eyes of Hashem like all the proper things that his father did, but not like his wickedness.
in the days of Zecharyah This refers to Uziyahu, and he was called by three names: Uziyahu, Zecharyah, and Azaryah, similar to (Melachim II 14): Yehoahaz/Achazyahu.
who understood the visions of Elokim who understood that the fear of Elokim is good, and feared Hashem.
And Uziyahu built towers, etc. He had to strengthen the parts of the wall they breached in his father’s days.
plowmen - Heb. אִכָּרִים, aratkori in Italian, plowmen.
for he loved the soil It is explained in Genesis Rabbah (See 22:3): Two had a passion for agriculture, and no good was found in them: he and Kayin.

engines, invented by skillful men - Heb. חִשְּׁבֹנוֹת מַחֲשֶׁבֶת חוֹשֵׁב, similar to (Shemot 28:6): “expert work (מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב.)” He made war engines with craftsmanship, such as siege mounds and battering rams, as it is written (Mishlei 24:6): “For you shall wage war with strategies.”

and he trespassed against Hashem, his Elokim - Heb. וַיִּמְעַל. Here it is appropriate to say מְעִילָה (trespass), for he sinned inadvertently, similar to (Vayikra 5:15): “If a person commits a trespass (תִמְעל מַעַל) and sins inadvertently.”
and he came into the Temple of Hashem for he said, “It is proper for a king to serve the King of glory.”
and in his hand was a censer to burn and he wished to strike the priest who prevented him from burning incense.

in a house of retirement Heb. בֵּית הַחָפְשִׁית. And in Yerushalmi (unknown) it is explained that he made himself a house in the cemetery, reminiscent of (Tehillim 88:6): “Among the dead, a free man (חָפְשִׁי) .”
for it had been decreed upon him to come no longer among people, similar to (Esther 2:1): “and that which was decreed upon her.”
in the cemetery but not in the cave with the kings.

as all that his father Uziyahu the good deeds that his father had done. That is what R. Shimon ben Yohai said in Tractate Sotah (sic. Should be Sukkah 45b): If Avraham would take upon himself all the sins of the generations until his time, I would take upon myself the sins of the generations from Avraham until my time. And if Yotam the son of Uziyahu were with me, we would take upon ourselves the sins of all the generations from Avraham until the end of all generations, for in all the kings before him and after him we find sin, except in Yotam. Concerning David it is written, (Melachim I 15:5): “Only concerning the matter of Uriyah the Chiti”; concerning Shlomo it is written, (ibid. 11:4): “His wives turned his heart away”; Rechavam forsook Hashem’s Torah; Aviyah (ibid. 15:3): “went in all his father’s sins”; Asa took silver and gold from the treasuries of the House of Hashem and put the prophet in prison; Yehoshafat associated with a wicked man (Achav and his son Achazyahu); Yoram killed his brother; Achazyahu’s mother advised him to sin; Yoash killed Zecharyah and was [later punished by being] sexually molested (Yer. Kid. 1:7); Amatzyahu prostrated himself before the graven images of Seir; Uziyahu entered the Temple to burn incense; Achaz went in the ways of the kings of Yisrael and also made monuments for the baalim; Chizkiyahu became haughty and there was anger upon him, and the sages did not concur with him on three things that he did (Pes. 4:9); Menashe did evil in the eyes of Hashem; Yoshiyahu did not heed the words of prophecy from Elokim; Tzidkiyahu did evil in the eyes of Hashem and did not humble himself before Yirmiyahu (below 36:12). In Yotam, however, no trace of sin was found. (R. Eliezer the son of Moshe told me this.)
the people were still acting corruptly as it is written in Melachim II (15:35): “the people were still slaughtering and burning incense [on the high places].”
and in the wall of the rampart - Heb. עֹפֶל, similar to (Yeshayahu 32:14): “rampart and tower (עפֶל וָבַחַן) .” He built strongholds.
and in the forests he built palaces - Heb. בִּירָנִית, an expression of a large palace (בִּירָה).
Ma'aseyah, the king’s son [I.e., the son of] Achaz. Zichri, a mighty man of Efraim slew [him].
and Azrikam - Heb. וְאֶת וְאֶת, similar to (Bereshit 36:24): “and Ayah and Anah (וְאַיָּה וְעַנָה),” and similarly, (Tehillim 76:7): “and chariot and horse (וָרֶכֶב וָסוּס) were stunned.”
And the men who were mentioned by name arose above (verse 12). Who were they? Those men who were of the heads of the sons of Efraim: Azaryah the son of Yehochanan and his colleagues.
and all their nakedness - Heb. מַעֲרֻמֵּיהֶם, an expression of (Yechezkel 15: “naked (עֵרם) and bare.”
And Plishtim raided the cities of the lowlands and the southland which was opposite them, as it is written about the Plishtim, (Tzefanyah 2:5): “the inhabitants of the seacoast.”
for he exposed Yehudah - Heb. הִפְרִיעַ, similar to (Shemot 32:25): “for Aharon had exposed them (פְּרָעֹה) (Jud. 5:2): “When breaches are made (בִּפְרֹעַ פְּרָעוֹת).”
came upon him for he had sent after him to aid him, as is written in Melachim II (16:7): “And Achaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pilneser.”
and oppressed him from that which he shared with him [from] the House of Hashem and the palace of the king, etc.”

but he was of no help to him Even though we find in II Kings (ibid. verse 9): “and the king of Ashur went up to Damesek and seized it and exiled it[s inhabitants] to Kir, and slew Retzin,” he was not much of an aid to him to strengthen him and to restore the cities that the Plishtim had taken from him.

and he closed the doors of the House of Hashem so that the priests would not go to perform their service in the Tent of Meeting, but come to the altars that he erected on every corner in Yerushalayim, and Chizkiyahu “opened the doors of the House of Hashem,” (below 29:3) because his father had closed the doors of the House of Hashem.
and reinforced them because Achaz had destroyed all the vessels of the House of Elokim.

and remove the ‘menstruant’ The Midrash Aggadah (source unknown) states: ‘The corpse’ is not stated here, but ‘the menstruant,’ which is more repugnant than the corpse. It is compared to the uncleanness of the menstruant, because menstrual blood is repugnant.

extinguished the lamps, and they did not burn incense nor offer up burnt offerings in the Sanctuary to the Elokim of Yisrael but they made high places to alien gods in every city, to burn incense to them.
do not forget - Heb. תִּשָּׁלוּ, an expression denoting lack of intention.
And the priests came within for the Leviyim may not enter within.
to the court of the House of Hashem the place where the Leviyim stood, as he says: “and the Leviyim received, etc.”

They commenced on the first of the first month etc., they sanctified the House of Hashem for eight days This is why they prolonged the cleansing to cleanse it so long, because Achaz had painted all the walls with images, as it is written (Yechezkel 23:14): “Images of Kasdim, engraved with types of drawings,” and they prolonged it for eight days until they destroyed the likeness of the images from the walls, and on the sixteenth day of the month, they completed everything, the Temple and the forecourt.

we have prepared and sanctified This is explained in Abodah Zarah (52b) in the chapter entitled “Rabbi Yishmael”: May vessels used in the Onias temple be used in the Temple?...He questioned him, “’That King Achaz forsook, etc....we have prepared and sanctified.’ Does not ‘we have prepared’ mean that they immersed them and ‘sanctified’ mean that they consecrated them?” He replied, “Blessed are you to Heaven, for you have restored my loss to me. ‘We have prepared’ means that we have concealed them and ‘sanctified’ means that we consecrated others in their stead.”
and seven kids, etc. This was a temporary provision.
on the altar of Hashem but not on those altars that his father Achaz had made.

to atone for all Yisrael for they had sinned by [practicing] idolatry. The king said as follows: “Let the burnt offerings and the sin offerings be for all Yisrael.” In the section שְׁלַח (Bamidbar 16:24) it is written: “the entire congregation shall offer up one bull, etc.,” and it is written: (Vayikra 4:14): “and the congregation shall bring a young bull for a sin offering,” and here it is written that they brought seven bulls, rams, lambs, and kids! This was a temporary ruling.

for by the hand of Hashem was the commandment, by the hand of His prophets that the Leviyim should play musical instruments. It is not written in the Torah that a sacrifice requires musical accompaniment (lit., song), but it is the commandment of Hashem, which He commanded through His prophets to accompany the sacrifice with song. Our Rabbis explained in Tractate Arachin (11a): From where do we derive that the Leviyim are required to play musical instruments? For it is written (Bamidbar 4:47): “the service of the service.” Which is a service that requires another service with it? This is music with a musical instrument. “And the service of raising” may also be correctly explained in reference to song, as it is written (Divrei Hayamim I 15:22): “And Knanyahu, the leader of the Leviyim in song (בְּמַשָּׂא) etc. because he was an expert,” for he was appointed to raise the voice of the melody of the song.
and the priests with the trumpets as it is written (Bamidbar 10:8): “And Aharon’s sons, the priests, shall blow the trumpets.”

to praise Hashem with the words of David and Asaf the seer i.e., “Give thanks to Hashem, call out in His name,” as is written above (Divrei Hayamim I 16:8f): “On that day, David placed Natan at the head to give thanks to Hashem by the hand of Asaf and his brethren, etc.”
and the congregation brought [peace] offerings and thanksgiving offerings which are permissible for the owner to eat.

and every generous-hearted one - burnt offerings Some of them, whoever was moved by his heart, brought burnt-offerings, but not all of them [i.e., not all the people brought burnt-offerings], because the owner has no permission to eat them.
And the sacred offerings sacred offerings of the lower degree - [thanksgiving-] offerings and peace-offerings, from which the owners may benefit.

Only the priests were few i.e., Those who had consecrated themselves were still few; so their kinsmen, the Leviyim, reinforced them until the work was completed and until the priests consecrated themselves. Now, should you ask: How was it that the Leviyim consecrated themselves and the priests did not consecrate themselves? Scripture explains: “for the Leviyim were more conscientious than the priests to consecrate themselves”; the Leviyim were more conscientious than the priests, for the priests and the Leviyim and all Hashem-fearing people had disguised themselves and made themselves appear unrecognizable, and had even hidden, all the days of the wicked kings, and when Chizkiyahu - who was righteous - came, they could not immediately consecrate themselves and cleanse themselves, for this was in the first year of his reign; so they came and consecrated themselves gradually, as it is written (Mishlei 28:12): “When the righteous rejoice, there is much glory, but when the wicked rise up, a person disguises himself,” and it is written (ibid. verse 28): “When the wicked rise up, people hide; but when they perish, the righteous increase.” When the wicked Achaz rose up, people hid, but when he perished, the righteous increased, i.e., Chizkiyahu and his company.

over that which Elokim had prepared for the people to serve Him and to do His will, similar to below (30:19): “His whole heart he set to seek, etc.,” and they also rejoiced because they were suddenly inspired in the first year of his reign to return to Hashem, and they returned immediately.

and he also wrote letters to Efraim and Menashe, etc. because they were not yet exiled, because this was in the first year of his reign and they were not exiled until the sixth year of his reign as it is written (Melachim II 18:10): “And they captured it at the end of three years, in the sixth year of Chizkiyahu, which was the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Yisrael,” as you will find at the end of the Book.
For they could not perform it at that time in the first month, in Nissan.

for the priests had not consecrated themselves sufficiently They had not consecrated themselves sufficiently for Yisrael to offer their Passover sacrifices, and it goes without saying that they could not perform it in Nissan, for they did not finish consecrating the Temple until the sixteenth of Nissan, but this is its meaning: For they could not perform it at that time; i.e., even if they had not delayed the purification of the Temple, which they did not complete until the sixteenth of Nissan, they would not have been able to perform it now [the offering of the Passover sacrifice] because not enough priests had consecrated themselves.
and the people had not gathered all of them [had not] yet [gathered] to Yerushalayim.
from Beer Sheva to Dan This is the boundary of the Ten Tribes.
because for many years The meaning is that many years had passed in which they had not performed it according to its law.

so that He may return to the remnant that has escaped from the clutches of the kings of Ashur Although they had not yet been exiled, he calls them a remnant that has escaped because they considered themselves as if they had already been exiled, and moreover, the kings of Ashur had seized everything in the days of Achaz, and the reason they saw themselves as if they had already been exiled was that for six years Bnei Yisrael were tribute-paying serfs to the king of Ashur, and he ruled over them and led them away into exile and did with them as he wished. This occurred within those six years, and they had already been exiled many times in the days of the kings of Yisrael and Achaz, and they knew that as soon as Yisrael would rebel against the king of Ashur, he would lead them away in exile. He calls them ‘those who escaped from Ashur’ because he ruled neither over them, nor over the entire land of Yehudah.

And do not be like your fathers or like your brothers The meaning is: Now if you say, “We still trust that the king of Ashur will withdraw from us,” do not be like your fathers, every generation that was before you. What happened to them when they forsook Hashem and acted treacherously? “He made them a desolation, as you see.”

For when you return to Hashem, your brothers and your sons will find compassion before their captors and shall return to this land Even those few who have already been exiled, for they waged war with Yisrael and they overwhelmed them, and they led their sons and daughters into captivity. But if you return to Him, He will grant them compassion before their captors, that they will return to this land, for Hashem your Elokim is gracious and merciful.
the altars for incense a place where there were priests and Leviyim.

and the priests and the Leviyim were embarrassed that they had delayed to consecrate themselves. They tarried so long and did not come until now for the following reason: they could not believe that this was true beforehand, because Achaz had dismissed them from officiating as priests. And so they said, “Is it possible that yesterday Achaz worshipped idols, and that his son Chizkiyahu, immediately in the first year and first month would tell the priests and Leviyim to worship the one God alone and have need of us?” They were therefore lazy and neglected to come, together with the rest of Yehudah, whom Achaz had dismissed. But when they investigated and understood that everything was for the name of Heaven, they all came and consecrated themselves.

the priests sprinkled For [the rituals] from the reception [of the blood] and onwards are the commandments of the priests, and do not wonder why the owners themselves did not slaughter [the sacrifices], as is explained further: for there were many among the congregation who had not consecrated themselves and the Leviyim presided over the slaughter of their Passover sacrifices.
for everyone who was unclean a Levi took his place to sanctify it for Hashem.
for they ate the Passover sacrifice not as it is written not in accordance with halachah, for they ate it in a state of uncleanness, for Chizkiyahu prayed for them, saying, etc.

who has set his whole heart So it is explained in the Baraitha of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Yosei the Galilean which commences: Wherever you find the words of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Yosei the Galilean in Aggadah, listen attentively, as it is said (Mishlei 2:2): “To make your ear attentive to wisdom” of the thirty-two methods by which the Aggadah is expounded, and this is one of them:. If the sequence was separated, e.g. this one: The good Hashem will atone for anyone who has set his whole heart to seek Elokim to perform His Passover sacrifice, to offer up his sacrifice—even though they did not offer it with the purity of sacred things, for they had not purified themselves; the entire Yehudah had purified themselves because they were near Yerushalayim, and they could cleanse themselves and consecrate themselves and return to Yerushalayim, but many from Efraim and Menashe, Yissachar and Zevulun were not so much to blame in the matter, because the matter was far away for them through letters, and they did not have time to wait and to delay their coming until they consecrated themselves. They therefore came and were not purified. And because it was not their fault, therefore atone for them. Similarly, (Yeshayahu 35:1f.): “Desert and wasteland shall rejoice over them, etc.”: the sequence is separated.
and the priests with powerful instruments with trumpets.

who were experts in the service of Hashem it is appropriate to use the term “expertise” (שֵׂכֶל) in regards to song, as it is written, (above Divrei Hayamim I 26:14): “And the lot to the east fell to Shelemyahu, and Zecharyah, his son, a prudent counselor, etc.,” (יוֹעֵץבְּשֵׂכֶל). Chizkiyahu spoke to their hearts with consolations and pleasant words to encourage them and assist them, in order that they too strengthen the song with expertise for Hashem.
and thanking Hashem over the thanksgiving offerings, and they thanked Hashem for the miracle that He had wrought for them, for the thanksgiving offering comes for a miracle.
another seven days as it is explained: and they kept seven days of joy.
separated from his small cattle and from his large cattle.
for the congregation one thousand bulls, etc. and they were eating together, the king, the officers, and the people, with joy.

for since the days of Shlomo the son of David, king of Yisrael, there had not been the like in Yerushalayim It is possible that a greater multitude had come for the festival to Yerushalayim in the days of Shlomo, but there had never been such a great rejoicing as this in Yerushalayim since the days of Shlomo. They were joyful about this [gathering], for if they had gathered in Yerushalayim on every festival, it would have been nothing new and they would have had no cause for [special] joy But now, since they had not performed the festival pilgrimage to Yerushalayim all the days of Achaz and the wicked kings of Yehudah, and they were now permitted to go up to Yerushalayim they rejoiced greatly. And since it was so many years since they had gone to Yerushalayim, the seven days of the Festival of Matzoth were too few in their eyes and they added another seven days in which to rejoice, and they rejoiced a great rejoicing.

and they blessed the people If you wish, you may say that they blessed them with this [blessing] that they begged to return from the land of their captors, and Hashem hearkened to their voice and returned them. Another possible explanation: and He hearkened to their voice, and so it is written above (v. 20): “and Hashem hearkened to Chizkiyahu and healed the people.”
each man according to his service the priests to minister, and the Leviyim to be singers and gate sentries, and every man at his proper service.
And the king’s portion from his possessions for the burnt-offerings, etc. which he (willingly) gave to perform them.

And he commanded the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, etc. in order that they be strengthened in the Law of Hashem with greater enthusiasm. Moreover, as long as their sustenance will be provided, they will be able to perform and occupy themselves with the Law of Hashem, because the Law was given only to those who ate manna, and secondly, to those who eat the heave-offering (Mechilta, Beshallach 17, Tanh. Beshallach 20).
And when the word burst forth from the king’s mouth to give a portion to the priests and the Leviyim, the Children of Yisrael increased the first of corn, wine, oil, honey date honey.

and all the increase of the field But all these [aforementioned] are not of the grain of the field, but so it is explained in Tractate Nedarim, in the chapter, “Whoever vows [to abstain] from herbs, is permitted to partake of pumpkins,” (55a): Rav Josef questioned: “And when the word burst forth, the Children of Yisrael increased, etc.” Now if you say that all these [i.e., all plants that are stacked up] are included in the term דָּגָן, what is the meaning of “when the word burst forth”? Replied Abbaye: This is to include fruit of trees and vegetables....Replied Rava: תְּבוּאָה (grain) is one thing, and תְּבוּאַת שָׂדֶה (increase of the field) is another.
and the tithes of sacred things consecrated to Hashem the tithe of the tithe, which the Leviyim give the priests (Bamidbar 18:25f.).
and they gave many stacks עֲרֵמוֹת עֲרֵמוֹת (houffen, Middle High German, heaps), an example is (Shir Hashirim 7:3): “a stack of (עֲרֵמַת) wheat.”

they commenced to lay the foundations of the stacks The beginning of anything is called a foundation, like the foundation of a house, which is the beginning of the structure, and like the verse in Ezra (7:9) “that is the commencement of (יְסֻד) the ascent, etc.”
and they blessed Hashem Who inspired Yisrael to separate their heave-offerings and their tithes.

And Chizkiyahu demanded Since Chizkiyahu saw that the stacks were large, he said to himself, “Perhaps the priests and the Leviyim have not taken [their share] from them and have not touched them, for had they touched them, how could they be so large? Since he was puzzled, he questioned them concerning the stacks, “What is the reason for this?”
And Azaryah...said to him He lived in the days of Uziyahu.

“From the beginning of bringing the heave-offering We have surely eaten, and not an incidental meal but we ate, were satisfied, and left over. Now what you are surprised about, that we ate four months, and nevertheless, their stacks are so large - this is because Hashem blessed His people and gave them abundant grains; therefore, they increased our heave-offerings and tithes.
and what is left over from this eating of ours.
is this abundance that you see: many stacks.
to prepare the chambers in the House of Hashem in which to deposit the heave-offerings.

And the priests who traced their genealogy to the house of their fathers, and the Leviyim with the genealogy of their infants, their wives, their sons, and their daughters. They would supply their sustenance from the heave-offerings and the tithes for that entire congregation. All these whom we mentioned [would supply food] to those who stood in the forecourt, and also to the sons of Aharon, the priests whose watch had not yet come about in which to minister, and who were in the field of the open land of their cities, in every city.

were men who were mentioned by names Above (verses 12ff.) Konanyahu and his brethren were appointed over them to receive the portions: the heave-offerings and the tithes from Bnei Yisrael to distribute the portions to every male among the priests and the Leviyim

to every male among the priests and also to their wives, their sons, and their daughters. The Chronicler says “to every male” here to teach something remarkable, i.e., they would provide even to the young male children, as above (verse 16): “of the males from three years old and over,” and they would surely provide for their wives, sons and daughters.

After these deeds of integrity, etc. and planned to make a breach therein - Heb. לְבִקְעָם like לְבָקְעָם like (Amos 2: “For selling (מִכְרָם) [an innocent man] for money,” like (מָכְרָם) and adjacent to that, (ibid. 1:13): “Because they ripped up (בִּקְעָם) the pregnant women of Gilad,” and its meaning and examples of it are (Yeshayahu 7:6): “and let us breach its walls (וְנַבְקְעֶנָה),” and (Bereshit 22:3): “Then he split (וַיְבַקַּע) wood for the burnt-offering.”
and he reinforced the millo An example is (Melachim I 11:27): “built the millo.”
and he made many swords - Heb. שֶׁלַח, weapons, similar to (above 23:10): “each one with his sword (שִׁלְחוֹ) in his hand”; (Nechemyah 4:17): “each man took his sword (שִׁלְחוֹ) to the water.”

In what do you trust It is written (Melachim I 18:5): “He trusted in Hashem Elokim of Yisrael,” and it is also written there: (verse 7) “and he rebelled against the king of Ashur.” Therefore, he asked, “In what do you trust” that you have rebelled against me?
stay in the siege in Yerushalayim as it is written (here): “to die by famine and thirst.”

Did not he - Chizkiyahu - who trusts in his Elokim, did he not transgress? Now even if He had the ability to help him, He would not help him, because he sinned against Him, for he removed His high places and His altars, saying to Yehudah and to Yerushalayim: Before one altar you shall prostrate yourselves Now is it not preferable that the Yehudim prostrate themselves before one altar and the Jerusalemites before one, or two and more? What does one altar avail such a large people?
