For they thought that all those high places that he had removed, as above (31:1): “and cut off the asherim, etc.” were built in the name of the Elokim of Yisrael.
whom my fathers destroyed Pul, the king of Ashur, and Tiglath-Pilneser.

And he wrote letters to blaspheme Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael And in Melachim II (19:14) and in Yeshayahu (37:14) it is written: “And Chizkiyahu took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read it; he went up to the House of Hashem, and Chizkiyahu spread it out before Hashem.”
with a loud voice in Yehudi, etc. to frighten them and to terrify them Here he relates the matter in generalities, but in Melachim II (19) and in Yeshayahu (37) it is thoroughly elaborated upon.
And they spoke of the Elokim of Yerushalayim The author of this Book complains about the villain Sancheriv, who blasphemed the living Elokim.

as of the gods of the peoples of the land which are the handiwork of man, and they compared the Elokim, our Maker, Who formed everything, to the gods of the peoples, who are their own handiwork, as is written above (v. 14): “Who is it among all the gods of, etc. that your Elokim should be able to save you from my hand?”
And Chizkiyahu... prayed In Melachim II (19:15–19) and in Yeshayahu (37:15–19) the prayer is delineated.
and some of his own issue as it is written (Yeshayahu 37:38): “and his sons slew him with the sword.”
and he prayed to Hashem as is delineated in Melachim II (20:3).
and he spoke to him What is the sign?
and he gave him a sign (ibid. verse 9ff.) “This is your sign, etc.” Everything is delineated there.
But...did not repay Him according to that which He had bestowed upon him Chizkiyahu did not repay the Holy One, blessed be He in accordance with that which He had bestowed upon him by healing him.
for his heart became haughty as it is written (ibid. 20:13): “and he showed them his entire treasure-house...and in all his kingdom.”
and there was wrath upon him and upon Yehudah and Yerushalayim because of this, and the author of this Book abridged it here because it is described in Melachim II (20) and in Yeshayahu (39).

And Chizkiyahu became humbled when his heart was haughty as it is written there: “And Chizkiyahu said to Yeshayahu: [The word of the Lord that you have spoken is] good.” And when he became humble, the wrath did not come upon them in his days.
and for all precious vessels he made various kinds of treasure-houses.

And storehouses for the increase Regarding storehouses of increase [of grain] it is appropriate to use the term מִסְכְּנוֹת, storehouses, in all places, like (Shemot 1:11): “store cities (עָרֵי מִסְכְּנוֹת) for Paroh,” and so, (above 8:4): “And he built Tadmor in the desert and all the store cities (עָרֵי מִסְכְּנוֹת) that he built in Chamat,” and perforce, they were for grain, because in the desert he did not have to store gold and silver.
and stalls for all kinds of beasts - Heb. וְאֻרָוֹת, large stables.
and he led them straight down on the west He led them along a straight way down on the west to the City of David.

And so, because of the emissaries of Heb. בִּמְלִיצֵי, messengers, similar to (Bereshit 42:23): “for the interpreter (הַמֵּלִיץ) was between them” because the messenger is the liaison between the sender and the one to whom he is sent. This is related to the verse that states: “and Chizkiyahu prospered in all his work,” and after all this good, which the Holy One, blessed be He, had bestowed on him, Elokim forsook him to test him, to know what was in his heart through the emissaries of the officers of Bavel, who were sent to him.
to seek the sign that was in the land He did not stand up to the test, and he showed them the weakness of his whole house. The verse is to be explained as if the phrases are reversed.
in the best - Heb. בְּמַעֲלֵה, in the best, as is explained at the end of the first chapter of Baba Kamma (16b).

“In Yerushalayim, My name shall be forever” Scripture decries Menashe, who built altars to pagan deities in the very House concerning which the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “I wish My name to rest there.” The verse stated after this (verse 7) is also an expression of decrying: “And he placed the graven image of the idol that he made in the House of Elokim, concerning which, etc.” And also the verse (8): “And I will not continue to remove Yisrael’s feet, etc.”

and those who divine by the jidoa bone - Heb. יִדְּעוֹנִי spelled in full with a “vav,” because he did much [evil], and he added to the graven image of the idol that he made. They would take the bone of an animal known as jidoa, and place it in their mouths, whence it would speak.
forever - Heb. לְעֵילוֹם, [a variant of] לְעוֹלָם.

And I will not continue to remove Yisrael’s feet This refers back to the above verse, and all is a complaint; i.e., the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “So I said to David and to Shlomo, ‘In this House I will place My name forever,’ and I also promised him, ‘And I will not continue to remove Yisrael’s feet from the land, if they will but observe, etc.’” But now And Menashe led astray, etc. Because of him the Shechinah departed, and we are also still in exile because of him.
of Gichon in the valley beside the valley of Gichon, the name of a place.
and he surrounded the Ofel And he surrounded from there the strength of the towers built with the work of Ofel.

and he cast them outside but he neither broke them nor hid them from the eye. Therefore, his son went astray after them, as it is written (below verse 22): “and to all the graven images that [Menashe his father] had made,” for he took them from the place where he had cast them.
and he sacrificed upon it peace-offerings and thanksgiving offerings He brought a thanksgiving offering and thanked the Holy One, blessed be He, for restoring him to Yerushalayim and to his kingdom.
and his prayer how he prayed.
and its acceptance and his return to his kingdom.
and they buried him in his house Like “in his house.” In Melachim II (21:18) it is written: “in the garden of his house.” He did not merit to be buried with his forefathers.

when he was still a youth, he started to seek The meaning is that although he was still a youth, he started to seek after the Elokim of David his father. This is similar to (Bereshit 37:2): “and as a youth, with the sons of Bilhah, etc., Yosef brought evil reports of them,” and this is not surprising, but if he were thirty years old, he would not have done it. It is, however, surprising, that he (Yoshiyahu) was a youth, and nevertheless, he started to seek, etc.

he started to purge Yehudah and Yerushalayim of the high places, the asherim that Menashe had made and that Amon his son had renewed, as above (33:3): “And he rebuilt the high places that Chizkiyahu his father had demolished, etc.”
and the sun images images of the sun.

that were above That they had placed above them, on high, opposite the sun, and they would prostrate themselves to it. Menashe had done all this, as it is written above (33:3): “and he prostrated himself to the entire host of the heaven, and he worshipped them.”

and he cast them upon the graves Here was fulfilled what he said to Yerovam, (Melachim I 13:2): “so said Hashem, ‘Behold a son will be born to the house of David, Yoshiyahu will be his name, and upon you will he sacrifice, etc., and human bones, etc.’”
And in the cities of Menashe and Efraim, etc. from those “gleanings” [survivors] who survived the sword and the captivity of Sancheriv.
with their instruments of destruction Since they were but few “gleanings,” they feared to live in the lowland and established their houses on the mountain (בְּחַר בָּתֵּיהֶם).

the recorder Wherever a scribe is mentioned, a recorder is mentioned in close proximity, for every king had a scribe to write everything that occurred in the kingdom, whether favorable or unfavorable, and he had a recorder sitting beside the scribe, to mention every incident, and the scribe would write according to what he told him.
which the Leviyim who guarded the threshold had gathered from the hands of Menashe and Efraim, etc. from their ruins round about.
to mend and repair - Heb. לִבְדוֹק. (Bereshit 42:9): “to see the nakedness (עֶרְוַת) of the land,” is translated into Aramaic as “to see the crack (בִּדְקָא)” of the land.
and wood for the couplings - Spangen in Middle High German, clasps.
and to make beams - Traver in Old French, to provide with beams.

to direct - Heb. לְנַצּחַ, lemestriyer, to direct, supervise, and so (Ezra 3:8): “to direct (לְנַצּחַ) the work of the House of the Lord,” and likewise (above 2:17): “and six hundred overseers (מְנַצּחִים) .”

and the Leviyim, all who were expert - Heb. מֵבִין. The term expertise (הֲבָנָה) is universally mentioned regarding song, and so above (Divrei Hayamim I 25:8), when they cast lots, it is written: “like the small one so the great one, expert (מֵבִין) with pupil.” And likewise, (ibid. verse 7): “trained in song to the Lord: every expert (מֵבִין),” and it is written (ibid. 15:22): “And Chananiah, the leader of the Leviyim, etc., because he was an expert (מֵבִין),” and he was appointed over them to chastise [them] in raising [the voice], how they should raise [their voice], because he was an expert (מֵבִין).
and of the Leviyim, scribes to write down the [amount of] silver brought to the House of Hashem and how they had collected it.
and officers over the work.
the Scroll of the Law of Hashem by the hand of Moshe the Book of Devarim.
and Chilkiyahu gave the scroll to Shafan because it was the scribe’s duty to read everything before the king.

and he further brought back word to the king for he first reported to the king about the errand that the king had sent him on to repair the House of Hashem his Elokim, as is written above (verse 8): “he sent Shafan the son of Atzalyahu, etc.”
And they poured - Heb. וַיַּתִּיכוּ, they poured, like (Bereshit 28:18): “and he poured (וַיִּצֹק) oil” and the Targum renders: וְאַתִּיךְ
And Shafan the scribe told the king After bringing back word to the king regarding his errand, he gave him the message of Chilkiyahu the priest, and read the scroll before him.

that he rent his garments When he heard them reading (Devarim 28:36): “Hashem will lead you and the king, etc.,” he interpreted [the following words] as referring to himself: “whom you will appoint over yourself.” The people had made him king, and he was not a prince by the word [of Hashem].

which has been poured upon us Since wrath is [compared to] fire, the term pouring applies to it, and a similar instance is below (verse 25): “My wrath shall be poured down upon this place, and it shall not be quenched.”
to Chuldah the prophetess Our Sages (Meg. 14b) explained that since a woman is more merciful than a man, he did not send them to Yirmiyahu the prophet.
the keeper of the raiment If you wish, you may say that this is either the priestly raiment or the royal raiment.

and she was sitting in Yerushalayim in the study-hall - Heb. בַּמִּשֶׁנֶה. The city had two walls, and she lived between the two walls. The Targum renders: in the study-hall. The meaning is: in the place of Torah, for Chuldah had a chamber adjacent to the Chamber of Hewn Stone. The Chamber of Chuldah was open to the outside and closed toward the Sanhedrin in the Chamber of Hewn Stone. So it is written in Tractate Middoth (unknown) because of modesty.

Say to the man He wished to interrupt the prophecy of the people “upon this place and upon its inhabitants,” and when he finished that prophecy, he then delineates, “And concerning the king of Yehudah, who sent you,” and he deals briefly with the prophecy of the palace and its inhabitants and puts it aside and focuses upon the prophecy of the king, which is long.

and you shall be gathered to your graves in peace But was he not slain? It [means] in peace from this, that your eyes will not see all the evil that I am bringing upon this place and upon its inhabitants, i.e., the destruction of the Temple.

the Scroll of the Covenant All the fright that the king experienced was due to the words (Devarim 28: 36): “Hashem will lead you,” and he saw that the Torah called it a covenant: “These are the words of the covenant.” Therefore, he too enacted a covenant and saw written immediately following it (ibid. 29:8): “And you shall keep the words, etc., and practice them.” Yoshiyahu also saw written immediately following (ibid. verses 9ff.): “You are standing today, all of you, etc....your children, your wives...that you should pass into the covenant...enacts with you today.” He said, “In such a manner, I too shall enact a covenant, for there it is written: ‘You are standing, etc.’ I too [will do so], ‘And he caused all those found in Yerushalayim, both small and great, to stand.’”
with all his heart and with all his soul as he found written there, (Devarim 30:2): “And you will return to Hashem your Elokim, etc. with all your heart and with all your soul.”
in his place An expression of נִצָּבִים, standing.

according to the covenant of Elokim, the Elokim of their forefathers According to all that which is written there: “the Elokim of their forefathers.” Therefore, it is written here, “the Elokim of their forefathers,” which He enacted for their forefathers in the desert. And every covenant that is there concerns idolatry, as it is written (Devarim 29:16f.): “And you saw their abominations and their depravities, etc....turns away today from Hashem.” Therefore, Yoshiyahu “removed all the abominations, etc.”
And Yoshiyahu made the Passover sacrifice in Yerushalayim since none of the wicked kings of Yehudah had made the Passover sacrifice according to its law.

Place the Holy Ark According to its simple meaning, [they were to return it to its place] because Menashe and Amon had removed the Holy Ark and placed their graven images in its place, as is proven above (33:7) concerning Menashe: “And he placed the graven image of the idol, etc.” Therefore, Yoshiyahu commanded to return it and to place the Ark in the place that Shlomo had built for it, but our Rabbis said (Yoma 42b) that he commanded the Leviyim to hide it there.

you have no burden on the shoulders This is another argument and the beginning of a statement. He said to them. You have no more toil of carrying a burden on your shoulders, i.e., all the vessels of the House of Hashem. You can no longer say, “Because of the toil of the burdens on our shoulders, we cannot serve Hashem and His people.” Therefore, from now on, serve Hashem your Elokim with song and His people Yisrael by slaughtering and flaying their Passover sacrifices, as is proven below (verse 6): “And slaughter the Passover sacrifice and prepare yourselves, etc.”
according to the divisions in divisions to make the Passover sacrifice according to its law, according to the word of Hashem by the hand of Moshe.
And Yoshiyahu separated for the members of the people - Heb. ויָּרֶם. An example is (Bamidbar 18: 28): “So shall you too separate (תָּרִימוּ),” an expression of separation.
for all that were present He separated small cattle for the Passover sacrifices for all Bnei Yisrael present.
for the number of thirty thousand of small cattle, of lambs, and goats.
and large cattle—three thousand for Festival peace offerings.
And they cooked the Passover sacrifice with fire according to the law Shemot 12:8): “Roasted with fire.”

and carried them quickly to all the members of the people [i.e.] the Leviyim [did this]; and after they had prepared for all Yisrael, the Leviyim prepared for themselves and for the priests, who did not have time to prepare.
the king’s seer Each one was a seer.

And such a Passover sacrifice had not been made In Melachim II (23:22) it is written: “For such a Passover sacrifice had not been performed since the time of the judges,” since the day that Yisrael was divided into two kingdoms, when the ten tribes separated from the kings of Yehudah and crowned a king over themselves. For all the time that they were two nations, the tribes of Yehudah and Binyamin made a Passover sacrifice for the sake of Hashem in Yerushalayim, and these [made one] for the sake of pagan deities in Beth-El and in Dan. And this did not occur all the days of the judges, until Yisrael was divided into two families, and every generation had only one judge, and that judge would compel them to walk in the way of Hashem, as is explained in Shoftim (2:18): “and Hashem was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge.” And all the ten tribes would go to Shiloh and make a Passover sacrifice for the sake of Hashem. But such a Passover sacrifice had not been made all the days of the kings of Yisrael and Yehudah, that they should make a Passover sacrifice together. But in the days of Yoshiyahu, when the kingdom of the ten tribes had already ceased to exist, for since Yirmiyahu had returned the ten tribes, they did not crown another king, but Yoshiyahu reigned over them, and they all made a Passover sacrifice together in Yerushalayim. This is the meaning of: “such a Passover sacrifice had not been performed...to Hashem in Yerushalayim.” This interpretation, however, misleads me very much, and does not appear correct to me, for although Yirmiyahu had returned the ten tribes and Yoshiyahu reigned over them in Yerushalayim, how is it possible that they did not make such a Passover sacrifice all the days of the judges and in the days of Shmuel the Seer and in the days of David and Shlomo, when Yisrael was dwelling in its land in peace and tranquility, and they had only one king, and their hearts were directed toward Heaven? Rather, this is the explanation, and this is the way Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Meshulam interpreted it to me: “And such a Passover sacrifice had not been made” ever, [it had never happened] that the king and the officers should supply enough animals for the Passover sacrifices and cattle for the festive peace offerings, and that he commanded the Leviyim to prepare for them and send each person according to how much he could eat.

After all this, that Yoshiyahu had prepared the Temple, Necho, the king of Mitzrayim, went up Scripture decries and laments Yoshiyahu, for a miracle was not performed for him as it had been for Chizkiyahu, about whom it is written (32:1): “After these deeds of integrity, Sancheriv the king of Ashur came” upon Chizkiyahu, and a miracle was performed for him.

went up to wage war in Karkemish on the Perat against the king of Ashur. So it is written in (II) Kings (23:29), and he wished to pass to him through the land of Yisrael, and Paroh Necho could not go to him by the way of the Perat River unless he were to pass through Yisrael, for Mitzrayim is south of the land of Yisrael, and the Perat River is north of the land of Yisrael.

went forth toward him for he interpreted (Vayikra 26:6): “and a sword will not pass through your land” to mean that even peaceful armies passing through the land [to attack other countries] should not pass through your land, but he was unaware of “the sin of the scorners of the generation, who arose to set up [idolatrous symbols] behind the door,” [i.e., he did not know that his generation found but little favor in God’s eyes], as is explained in Tractate Taanith (22b)

and he did not hearken to the words of Necho from the mouth of Elokim who said to him from the mouth of Elokim, for so said Yeshayahu, (19:2): “And I will stir up Mitzrim against Mitzrim.” This is what the Kallir composed: “He withheld his troops from marching to Aram Naharaim, in order that no single sword should pass through Efraim; and he did not hearken to the prophet to turn back, for it was decreed that Mitzri be set against Mitzri.”

into his second chariot for it was customary for the king to ride on two chariots; he rode mainly on the first, but if necessary, he would ride on the second. The first one went before them, and when he was stricken, they put him into the second chariot.

And all the male...singers - הַשָּׁרִים, an expression of song, choristers, for both song and lamentation are recited with the same voice. Concerning him, Amos prophesied (8:9): “and I will cause the sun to set at midday, and I will darken the land on a sunny day.” This is the day of Yoshiyahu, who died at the age of thirty-nine, in the middle of his days, for it is written (Tehillim 90:10): “The days of our years because of them are seventy years,” and it is written (Amos 8:10): “And I will turn your festivals into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation, etc. and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.” This is what [the Chronicler] says: “And all the male and female singers said in their lamentations,” “and all of Yehudah and Yerushalayim were mourning” for him.

and they made them a statute When any grief or weeping befalls them, for which they lament and weep, they mention this grief with it. An example is the Ninth of Av, in which we recite lamentations for those slain in the persecutions that occurred in our times. They will similarly bewail the day of Yoshiyahu’s death. An example is (Jud. 11:39f.): “and it became a statute in Yisrael, etc. to lament the daughter of Yiftach the Giladi, four days in a year.”
and behold, they are written in the lamentations in the Book of Eichah.

and his kind deeds And in Melachim II (23:25) it is written: “Now, before him there was no king like him.” This is what is stated here: “Behold they are written in the Book of the Melachim of Yisrael and Yehudah.”
and made him king instead of his father although Yehoyakim his brother was twenty-one months his senior.
And the king of Mitzrayim deposed him in Yerushalayim This is explained thoroughly in Melachim II (23: 33): “And Pharaoh-Neco imprisoned him in Rivlah in the land of Chamat.”
in Yerushalayim from reigning in Yerushalayim.
and he imposed a fine upon the land to give taxes. An example is (Devarim 22: 19): “And they shall fine him one hundred pieces of silver.”

and he changed his name to Yehoyakim It is the custom of kings and princes to bestow a by-name upon their servants as they wish. An example is (Bereshit 41:45): “And Paroh named Yosef, etc.,” and so (Bamidbar 13:16): “and Moshe called Hoshea the son of Nun, Yehoshua,” and so, (Daniel 1:7): “Now the chief officer gave them names, etc.” All this is to make known that he rules over him to name him as he desires.

and he changed his name to Yehoyakim Why did he change his name to Yehoyakim? It is explained above that after Paroh slew Yoshiyahu, he appointed a king and fined them by imposing a tribute of enslavement upon them.

Nevuchadnetzar the king of Bavel advanced upon him because Paroh could not go forth from his land, as it is written (Melachim II 24:7): “And the king of Mitzrayim no longer went out of his land, for the king of Bavel had taken from the river of Mitzrayim until the Perat River, all that belonged to the king of Mitzrayim,” for he defeated him in the fourth year in Karkemish on the Perat River, as is delineated in Yirmiyahu (46:2).

to bring him to Bavel He did not actually bring him, however, but he died on the way, and they cast away his corpse, and so did Yirmiyahu prophesy (22:19): “A donkey’s burial shall he be buried, dragged and tossed past the gates of Yerushalayim.” Now where is a donkey’s burial? In a dog’s stomach, and so it is apparent in Melachim II (24:6): “And Yehoyakim slept with his forefathers,” but it is not written: “and they buried him.”

And some of the vessels of the House of Hashem And some of the vessels of the House of Hashem, and concerning this, Yirmiyahu prophesied (27:21): “For so said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael, concerning the vessels remaining, etc.” Seder Olam questions (Daniel 1:1): “In the third year of the reign of Yehoyakim, king of Yehudah, etc. and Hashem delivered...into his hand.” Here, however, it is apparent that it was in the eleventh year of his reign. Now what is the meaning of “in the third year”? Counting from his rebellion, for it is stated (Melachim II 24:1): “and Yehoyakim was his vassal for three years, then he turned and rebelled against him” for three years, and in the third year of his rebellion, he advanced against him, and that is the eighth year of Nevuchadnetzar, for the master taught: In the first year [of his reign] he conquered Nineveh; in the second year he vanquished Yehoyakim, who served him for three years and rebelled against him for three years, and he did not reign until the fourth year of Yehoyakim, for it is stated (Yirmiyahu 25:1): “in the fourth year of Yehoyakim, the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah - that was the first year of Nevuchadnetzar.”
and the abominations that he was intimate with his mother.
and that which was found upon him This alludes to a tattoo, [something found on the body].
And at the return of the year that Yehoyakim was exiled.

with the precious vessels of the House of Hashem the desirable things. Those he took, and the rest he left until the exile of Tzidkiyahu. Then he took everything with him. And in Melachim II (24:12), it is explained that “Yehoyachin, the king of Yehudah, came out to the king of Bavel, etc.”

and he made Tzidkiyahu his brother king Yehoyakim’s brother, and so in Melachim II (24:17), “And the king of Bavel crowned Matanyah his uncle in his stead and changed his name to Tzidkiyahu,” Yehoyachin’s uncle.

And he did that which was evil in the eyes of Hashem What is the evil? That he did not humble himself before Yirmiyahu the prophet, [who spoke] from the mouth of Hashem, as is explained in Yirmiyahu (38:17ff.): “And Yirmiyahu said to Tzidkiyahu, ‘So said Hashem Elokim of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: If you go out, etc.’...’I fear the Yehudim, etc.’” But aside from this sin, he did not sin except insofar as he did not obey the words of the prophet speaking from the mouth of Hashem, and that he transgressed Nevuchadnetzar’s oath. But he did not do “his abominations and that which was found in” Yehoyakim, i.e., the evil done by Yehoyakim. [This was heard] from Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Meshulam.

who adjured him by Elokim as is explained in Yechezkel (17:12): “Say now to the rebellious house, etc.” The entire chapter was written regarding Yehoyachin and Tzidkiyahu: (verse 13f.) “took its king and its princes, and brought them to him to Bavel,” refers to Yehoyachin and his company. “And he took of the royal seed and formed a covenant with him,” refers to Tzidkiyahu.

Also, all etc. They should have instructed Yisrael, as it is written (Devarim 24:8): “in accordance with all that the priests, the Leviyim, instruct you.” This does not refer to simple priests, who have no power to protest, but to the chiefs of the priests, who have the power to protest, but they did not protest.
and they defiled the House of Hashem with their abominations.
which He had hallowed in Yerushalayim to cause His glory to rest there forever.

And Hashem...sent upon them All this is an acknowledgment of divine justice, so that you should not say that He did not forewarn them to repent of their evil ways, as it is written: “grasped forever His anger and kept His fury forever (Amos 1:12).” Therefore, it is stated: “And Hashem Elokim of their forefathers sent upon them through His messengers,” and forewarned them to repent of their evil, and not once a year or a month, but every day, “sending them with every fresh morn.”
for He had pity on His people and did not desire their death.
and on His abode on the abode of the Temple, for even a flesh and blood king has pity on his people and on his abode, not to destroy them.
But they mocked the messengers of Elokim the messengers of the Holy One, blessed be He.

and despised His words [The words] of the Holy One, blessed be He, for surely He is just. No one mocks even messengers of a flesh and blood [king] and they are afraid to transgress his command, whether for bad or for good, but His people despised His words and mocked and scoffed at His messengers, etc.

And He brought upon them the king of the Kasdim who were a lowly nation, as it is said (Yeshayahu 23:13): “Behold the land of the Chaldees, this people has never been,” and here was fulfilled (Devarim 32:21): “They provoked Me with a non-god, etc....I will provoke them to anger with a vile nation.”

and he slew their young men by the sword in their Temple and their recompense was requited them, as is written above (verse 14): “and they defiled the House of Hashem,” and that which He said was fulfilled, (Yechezkel 9:5ff.): “’and smite, let not your eye spare, etc....and go out,’ and they went out and smote in the city.”

and he had pity neither on youth nor virgin, elder nor ancient one unlike the custom of soldiers, who, when they are victorious in war, slay the combatants, but pity the elders, the youths, and the virgins, and are filled with compassion for them, and Moshe’s prophecy was fulfilled (Devarim 32:25): “The sword will bereave from outside and terror from within, youth, etc.”
And all the vessels of the House of Elokim, both large and small which were left over from the exiles of Yehoyakim and Yechonyah.

and they became vassals to him and to his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Paras And why until the kingdom of Paras? Because until that time, the land was not appeased for its Sabbaths, as it is written (Vayikra 26:35): “As long as it is desolate, it will rest.”
until the land was appeased for its Sabbaths Because prior to that, the land was not appeased for its Sabbaths.

all the days of its desolation it rested until the completion of seventy years [corresponding to] the Sabbatical and Jubilee years that Yisrael had neglected to observe in the land, and corresponding to them they were exiled for seventy years. The land of Yisrael rested for those seventy years. Bnei Yisrael provoked [God] in their land for 430 years. These included 390 years from the time they entered the land until the ten tribes were exiled therefrom, and they are explained (as follows): 243 years from the time Yerovam ascended the throne until Hoshea the son of Elah was exiled, and 111 years during the administration of the judges, when they provoked [Him], and the rest are obscure. That is what is stated in Yechezkel (4:4ff.): “And you shall lie on your left side, and you shall place the iniquity of the house of Yisrael, etc., 390 days, etc. And when you complete these, you shall lie on your right a second time, and you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Yehudah, 40 days, a day for a year, a day for a year.” This teaches that the house of Yehudah sinned from the time that the ten tribes were exiled until Yerushalayim was destroyed, for 40 years. How so? Twenty-two years of Menashe, as it is written (Melachim II 21:3): “according to all that Achav did,” and Achav reigned 22 years (and he [Menashe] repented for thirty-three years, totaling fifty-five years.) Add 2 years of Amon, and 11 of Yehoyakim, totaling thirty-five years, and this prophecy was transmitted to Yechezkel in the 5th year of Tzidkiyahu, totaling 40 years. The sum total of them all, of both Yisrael and Yehudah, is 430 years. Note that there are 64 Sabbatical and Jubilee years in 400 years. There are 5 Sabbatical years in 35 years, totaling 69, and the last Jubilee year was counted for them as iniquity, for because of their iniquity they were exiled therefrom. Hence the 70 hallowed years of Shemittah that Yisrael did not observe. They were consequently exiled for seventy years to fulfill what was said, (Vayikra 26:34): “Then the land will be appeased regarding its Sabbaths.” So it is explained in Seder Olam (see ch. 26). Chronicles is concluded with this since he says: “until the completion of seventy years.” He had to state these verses and those of Ezra (in the beginning) to let us know that when those seventy years were over, “the wheel rotated” and they returned to their land. He therefore said here: “in the first year of Koresh, the king of Paras” until “Who among you is of all His people, etc., and he may ascend.” The reason that the “vav” [and] of “And in the first year” is added, is because the Book of Daniel intervenes, for the book of Ezra continues in sequence after the Book of Daniel, and this “vav” connects them together.”
the spirit of Koresh his will.
and he issued a proclamation lie made an announcement to all his subjects.
and also in writing He sent to all his subjects, saying.
So said Koresh, the king of Paras, All the kingdoms of the earth For I reign as king over all the kingdoms.

and He commanded me And He commanded me through Yeshayahu to build Him a House in Yerushalayim, as it is said (Yeshayahu 44:2845:1): “Who says of Koresh, etc. So said Hashem to His anointed one, to Koresh.” And this prophecy of Yeshayahu had already been said to him.
which is in Yehudah Yerushalayim is in the provinces of Yehudah.

Who among you is of all His people, may Hashem his Elokim be with him, and he may ascend So was the proclamation to the provinces: Whoever is of the people of the Holy One, blessed be He, may come to build His House, which is in Yerushalayim.
and he may ascend and may the Holy One, blessed be He, help him and us.
